We're also located near the area’s most frequented destinations, including WakeMed Cary Hospital, Research Triangle Park and universities such as Duke, UNC Chapel Hill, NC State and more.

properties.name: Sonesta ES Suites Raleigh Durham Airport
properties.description: A renovated hotel offering comfort and convenience, Sonesta ES Suites Raleigh Durham Airport is conveniently located off Interstate 40, just one mile from RDU International Airport via complimentary airport shuttle service, and features spacious guest suites, breakfast and an evening social hour. Guests will find themselves located near Research Triangle Park (home to over 100 companies including Kendle, Lenovo, RH Donnelley and Tekelec), Wake Competition Center and other area destinations. This property is designed for an extended stay, offering separate sleeping, with updated living and dining areas. With full kitchens, living rooms with pull-out sofa beds and work desks with high speed Internet access, this hotel provides the comforts of home. Grab complimentary daily breakfast in the morning and mix and mingle at the nightly social hours. Meeting space is available for small meetings, training workshops and events. Sonesta ES Suites also offers preferred pricing for groups or guests staying for extended time at this Morrisville hotel.

properties.name: Sonesta Select Raleigh Durham Airport
properties.description: The newly renovated Sonesta Select Raleigh Durham Airport in Morrisville is located at the heart of the Triangle, nestled between Research Triangle Park, Cary and Brier Creek. Our hotel provides easy access to many area destinations, including the PNC Arena, Wake Competition Center, Raleigh Convention Center and North Carolina State Fairgrounds. Take advantage of our complimentary 24-hour airport shuttle service when flying in and out of Raleigh-Durham International Airport. Planning a meeting? Host it in one of three meeting rooms at Sonesta Select.

properties.name: SpringHill Suites Raleigh Apex
properties.description:
Experience unexpected extras during your stay at Springhill Suites by Marriott Raleigh - Apex, a brand-new, all-suite hotel that seamlessly blends design and functionality. Make the most of your trip with access to local attractions and complimentary onsite parking, featuring electric car charging stations. We're located two miles from the charming town of Apex and just 20 minutes from Research Triangle Park. North Carolina State University is conveniently nearby. After a long day, rest in spacious suites furnished by West Elm. Uncluttered and stress-free, featuring complimentary Wi-Fi and guest laundry, our suites will allow guests to stay productive while enjoying the comfort of modern amenities. Refresh in our fitness center and relaxing indoor pool. Unwind and grab a drink at the lobby bar. Our market is open 24/7 for snacks and necessities. Enjoy our complimentary breakfast with fresh choices for a customized start to your day. From business trips to leisurely journeys, SpringHill Suites is a breath of fresh air.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Staybridge Suites Raleigh-Durham Apt-Morrisville
properties.description: Staybridge Suites Raleigh-Durham Apt Morrisville provides everything you need for an extended stay or just one night. This property will make you feel welcome with the home-like surroundings and amenities. The suites have a full kitchen with residential size refrigerator, stove top and dishwasher. Complimentary full breakfast buffet, on-site self laundry room and social reception, Tues.-Thurs. evenings will make your stay even more enjoyable. This pet friendly hotel features a wonderful outdoor area with a sport court, grills and outdoor seating with fireplace.

properties.name: Suburban Extended Stay Hotel
properties.description: When you’re in need of a long-term hotel, Suburban Extended Stay Hotel offers a place to stay that won’t break the bank. We provide basic amenities like free WiFi, free coffee and free parking. Stay productive in the business center featuring an Internet-connected computer and print station. Our 100% smoke-free hotel also offers a lounge/bar, exercise room, outdoor seasonal pool, bottled water and hotel safe. And you’ll always get professional service from our friendly staff and 24-hour reception.

properties.name: Super 8 by Wyndham Raleigh North East
properties.description:
Conveniently located in northeast Raleigh and close to many attractions, Super 8 by Wyndham Raleigh North East is just five miles from Downtown Raleigh. Easy access to nearby businesses and attractions such as Falls Lake, Adventure Landing, Triangle Town Center and Lafayette Village shops and restaurants. 

Feel at home with everything you need for a great stay. Enjoy newly renovated Guestrooms,  View premium high-definition channels on a 32-inch LCD TV. Take advantage of free WiFi, refrigerator and microwave in each room for your convenience.

properties.name: Tempo by Hilton Raleigh Downtown (Opening Winter 2024)
properties.description: Relax and recharge in The Tempo by Hilton Wellness Rooms with Peloton. Designed with everything you need to power up, prep for the day, and maintain your wellness routine while on the road. Our rooms are a beat ahead — havens that help you unwind, unplug, and fall asleep faster. The bath suite is bright and spacious with a premium shower experience and elevated design features. Spread out in the Get Ready Zone, a flexible space to get organized, fuel up, or get some work done. Experience The Tempo by Hilton Wellness Rooms, featuring a Peloton spin bike and products from Therabody, so you can workout at your own pace while on the road.

properties.name: SpringHill Suites Raleigh Garner (Opening Winter 2024)
properties.description:
Travel in style at SpringHill Suites Raleigh Garner, a brand-new all-suite hotel that seamlessly blends design and functionality, offering the modern amenities you need just 6 miles from downtown Raleigh. Conveniently located off Interstate 40, we're close to an array of attractions that our guests love. Catch a movie at White Oak Crossing or enjoy live performances at the Garner Performing Arts Center. Explore the natural beauty of White Deer Park Nature Center or dive into culture at the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences and History. Don't miss a concert at the Coastal Credit Union Music Park or the Red Hat Amphitheater. For art lovers, the North Carolina Museum of Art is a must-visit, and the NC State Fair Grounds and the North Carolina Farmers Market offer unique local experiences. Our clean and spacious suites provide flexible spaces perfect for working, meeting, or relaxing, making your stay as stress-free as possible.

properties.name: Temporary Living Company
properties.description: Temporary Living Company is a premier provider of furnished and unfurnished temporary housing in the Raleigh area. Their portfolio of apartments, luxury condos and executive homes are near medical centers, RTP, recreation sites and colleges and universities. Privately owned and headquartered in Raleigh, Temporary Living Company's furnished and unfurnished housing options provide the convenience of a hotel with all the comfort of home. Temporary Living looks forward to helping make your short-term stay in N.C. a pleasant one!

properties.name: The Casso Raleigh
properties.description: Access the best of the North Carolina capital while enjoying the contemporary comforts of The Casso, centrally-located in the middle of the trendy downtown Warehouse District and Glenwood South. Featuring interior designs inspired by the local area, our non-smoking, dog-friendly retreat is within walking distance of shops, restaurants, museums, and parks and a quick 20 minute drive from the Raleigh-Durham International airport.

properties.name: The Longleaf Hotel
properties.description: The Longleaf Hotel is a modernized mid-century gem sitting at the northern gateway to downtown Raleigh not far from, well, everything. Our namesake, the soaring longleaf pine, has inspired every aspect of our modern renovation of this vintage motor lodge.

properties.name: The StateView Hotel
properties.description: The Stateview Hotel provides an innovative, vibrant guest experience driven by state-of-the-art technology, interactive spaces and the spirit of the N.C. State Wolfpack. The hotel’s university roots evoke both a sense of honoring the past and a collaborative, advanced look toward the future. Located on the serene setting of the shores of Lake Raleigh, the StateView provides an unmatched outdoor experience surrounded by a protected forest and walking trails, combining to create a guest experience unlike anything else in Raleigh.

properties.name: The Umstead Hotel and Spa
properties.description:
The Umstead Hotel and Spa is a singular, sophisticated triumph in N.C.'s northeastern Piedmont region. The state’s most highly rated hotel, it boasts stunning interiors punctuated with privately curated fine art, 150 spacious guest rooms and suites, world-class cuisine, a stimulating spa, gracious staff and a serene woodland setting.
The six-story hotel is nestled against a three-acre lake and resides on 12 acres. The hotel is six minutes to RDU International Airport, 10 minutes to PNC Arena and 15 minutes to downtown Raleigh or Research Triangle Park.
Room amenities include balconies, deep soaking bathtubs, bathrobes, bathroom amenities, clothes press, Nspresso machines, flat screen smart TVs, connecting rooms, versatile desks and seating, in room tablet controls, mini bars with local offerings, refrigerators, safes, separate showers and water closets, stereo systems, smoke detectors, touch panel lighting.

properties.name: TownePlace Suites Cary Weston Parkway
properties.description: Extended Stay/Select Service. TownePlace Suites offers uncomplicated residential living with your budget in mind. This town-house style community provides spacious studios, one- and two-bedroom suites, fully equipped kitchens, large work spaces with two phone lines, personalized voicemail and on-site business services, plus 24-hour staffing and housekeeping based on length of stay. Located at the intersection of Evans Rd. and Weston Pkwy.

properties.name: TownePlace Suites by Marriott Raleigh-University Area
properties.description: TownePlace Suites by Marriott® is an extended-stay hotel where you can balance work and life as you like, with the comfort, flexibility and affordability you require. Relax and feel at home with a fully equipped kitchen and high-speed Internet access.

properties.name: Tru by Hilton Raleigh Durham Airport
properties.description:
Say hello to a brand-new hotel experience from Hilton that’s vibrant, affordable and young-at-heart. It’s energetic, yet relaxing and comfortable. It’s     familiar, and it’s also unexpected. It’s uniquely Tru. 

Mix it up with board games in the lobby, a workout in the fitness center or chill time on our outdoor patio. Tru by Hilton Raleigh Durham Airport features  rooms with a king or two queen beds and a 55-inch HDTV with premium channel lineup. Nip any craving with drinks, gourmet snacks and single-service wine and beer in the 24/7 market and don’t forget about our free breakfast bar each morning.

We’re conveniently located in the heart of the Triangle with easy highway access to universities, shopping and the world-renowned Research Triangle Park.

Our Tru hotel is just 15 minutes to downtown Raleigh and less than 2 miles from Raleigh-Durham International airport. We also offer complimentary shuttle service to and from RDU.

properties.name: TownePlace Suites Raleigh-Durham Airport/Morrisville
properties.description:
Settle in for a comfortable extended stay at our brand new TownePlace Raleigh Durham Airport Morrisville, our new hotel located in the Research Triangle, minutes from Raleigh-Durham International Airport, between Downtown Raleigh and Downtown Durham, USA Baseball National Training Complex and Lenovo Headquarters. Explore an extensive network of hiking trails, lakes, and fishing at William B. Umstead State Park, or test your fitness at Triangle Rock Club. After your fun-filled day of hiking, rafting, or climbing, our relaxing suites await. Our fully equipped kitchens, free breakfast, free parking, and pet friendly offerings make for an unbeatable value. Explore more for less when you stay at our Raleigh-Durham Airport Hotel

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: WaterWalk Raleigh – RTP Extended Stay Suites
properties.description: Immerse yourself in Southern hospitality in the center of one of the country’s well-known technology and research communities. WaterWalk Raleigh RTP features modern furnished and unfurnished accommodations with an abundance of amenities. Choose to kick back and watch your favorite shows with our DirecTV package with over 200 channels including premium channels. Or, entertain guests in your contemporary, fully-equipped kitchen. Sit outside by the fire pit, cook out on ready-to-use gas grills or meet your neighbors at the lobby coffee bar or media room. The surrounding area boasts the nation’s largest research park, Research Triangle Park, home to more than 300 companies. Follow your curiosity to historic landmarks, museums and renowned universities like N.C. State. Hospitality is our passion.

properties.name: Wingate by Wyndham State Arena Raleigh/Cary
properties.description: Minutes from Research Triangle Park, PNC Arena, and NC State Fairgrounds! Conveniently located off I-40 and less than 15 minutes from the downtown area, we provide everything you need to make your stay more relaxed. Swim in the indoor pool or stay active in the 24-hour fitness center. Wake up to a free hot breakfast and use free WiFi to catch up on email.

properties.name: WoodSpring Suites Morrisville Raleigh Durham Airport
properties.description:
When your plans include an extended stay for a week, month or longer, WoodSpring Suites® Morrisville - Raleigh Durham is an extended stay hotel located close to the major cities of Raleigh and Durham. When you’re planning a quick visit or a longer stay, our accommodations are designed for guests looking for accommodations that help them feel at home. Each furnished suite includes an in-room kitchen—complete with microwave, full-size refrigerator and freezer, 2-burner cooktop and prep sink. Amenities include free WiFi, free parking, an onsite laundry facility, a fitness center and vending machines.

Our extended stay hotel is located 2 miles from Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU) and the Research Triangle Park. Business travelers are close to major companies such as Lenovo, Oracle, SAS, Cisco and Bayer. Sports teams and spectators appreciate our convenient location to Wake Competition Center, Triangle Aquatic Center, Hoop City U and USA Baseball. Several restaurants are close to our hotel, including Babymoon Café, Dim Sum House and Spinner Bar and Restaurant.

properties.name: WoodSpring Suites Raleigh Apex
properties.description:
The WoodSpring Suites® Raleigh Apex provides a convenient extended stay hotel for business travelers, military families, medical professionals, students and people relocating to the Raleigh area. Choose from three room designs, each with double/full-sized beds and sleeper sofas, free WiFi and full in-room kitchens. Relax in your room after a long day at work by making your own meals with groceries from nearby Lowes Foods or the Walmart Supercenter. Or choose from a variety of restaurants close to the hotel, including Chef’s Palette, Chili’s Bar and Grill, Zaxby’s, Olive Garden, Apex Wings Restaurant and Pub, Subway, IHOP and TGI Fridays.

This hotel offers weekly or monthly rates designed to help you save money the longer you stay, with amenities such as laundry facilities, free parking, vending machines and a friendly staff available to help 24 hours a day. Housekeeping services are provided every other week for long-stay guests.

properties.name: WoodSpring Suites Raleigh Northeast Wake Forest
properties.description: If you need a relaxing room in Raleigh for several nights or several months, book a stay at the WoodSpring Suites® Raleigh Northeast Wake Forest. At this extended stay hotel, you’ll enjoy apartment-style living and convenient amenities. Comfortable suites come equipped with double- or full-sized beds and in-room kitchens with full-sized refrigerators. You’ll also have access to conveniences like free parking, free WiFi and access to our guest laundry room. Housekeeping services are provided every other week for long-stay guests. Conveniently located near U.S. Route 1 and Interstate 540, our hotel is within minutes of plenty of grocery stores, restaurants and popular local attractions. Nightly, weekly and monthly hotel rates available!

properties.name: stayAPT Suites Raleigh-Durham/RTP
properties.description: stayAPT Suites Raleigh-Durham/RTP offers 500+ square feet suites with a dedicated living room, full kitchen and separate bedroom. From enjoying your morning coffee and breakfast in the kitchen to walking down the hall and getting ready for the day in the bedroom and separate bathroom, we’ve created an environment where guests can go about their day as if they were at home and not a hotel.

properties.name: HighPark Nail Spa
properties.description: HighPark Nail Spa offers beautiful nail services in Raleigh. The luxurious yet affordable manicures and pedicures will keep your hands and feet looking stunning. The salon takes sanitation seriously; tools are cleaned using an autoclave and a sheer ventilation system is used that keeps the spa's air fresh and free from strong odors typically found in nail salons. HighPark Nail Spa takes pride with having well trained and courteous associates that will assist you throughout your stay. Indulge yourself with nail and foot massage services in Raleigh!

properties.name: Salon Twenty One
properties.description:
Your style sets the tone for the rest of your life - at Salon 21, they know your hair speaks volumes about your style. Salon 21's award-winning stylists stay up on the latest trends - and work with you to find the manageable, contemporary style that shouts out who you want to be.

Photo Credit:

properties.name: Ruckus Pizza, Pasta, & Spirits - Morrisville
properties.description: Pizza, Pasta, Spirits and Sushi. The Most award winning restaurant in the Triangle 6 years in a row. Join Ruckus at any of our locations for a great Meal and a great time. Located in the Park West Village shopping center.

properties.name: Jimmy V's Osteria + Bar
properties.description:
Jimmy V's is a unique and modern restaurant created with Jim Valvano's passion and commitment to excellence, with 2.5% of the restaurant's revenue being donated to the V Foundation for Cancer Research. Since opening in 2013 Jimmy V’s has donated over $225,000 to help find a cure for cancer.


Jim Valvano's love for food is the influence behind the menu creation featuring local and seasonal dishes with an emphasis on delicious Italian/American cuisine. Executive chef Tom Stagikas and his team pride themselves on offering down to earth and traditional comfort foods using local farm grown ingredients and straightforward preparations.


Jimmy V's Osteria + Bar's concept is a warm and inviting ambiance for family gatherings, a night on the town or toast drinks with friends. The restaurant is also known for having downtown Raleigh's largest outdoor covered patio complete with a 10’ projection screen making it the ideal location to catch a Wolfpack game!

properties.name: Brixx Wood Fired Pizza - Brier Creek
properties.description: Brixx is the spot for families and friends to come together to enjoy each other while feasting on wood fired fare, salads, pasta, craft beer and wine. Their fresh ingredients and fine dining techniques meet everyday, casual food so you can sit back and connect in comfort. Vegan or gluten-free? Worry not — Brixx believes everyone should be able to go out for delicious food, regardless of dietary differences.

properties.name: Jefferson L. Sugg Farm at Bass Lake
properties.description:
The Sugg Farm parkland is open for special events. The Town's annual Spring Fling, July 5th celebration and HollyFest are held on the property. The property features several structures, including a horse stable and the previous owner's home. The land also provides connectivity to Bass Lake Park, an existing parks and recreation facility.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Lake Raleigh
properties.description: Cut into the southern side of Centennial Campus and surrounded by a protected forest, Lake Raleigh offers a picturesque retreat from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Open to the public, this 75-acre lake features a fishing pier and boat ramp for non-motorized watercraft, such as kayaks and canoes. Fish in the lake include largemouth bass and catfish.

properties.name: Lake Crabtree
properties.description: Lake Crabtree is a reservoir located in Cary, North Carolina. Constructed in 1989 by the Natural Resources Conservation Service through the damming of Crabtree Creek, it was designed to alleviate flooding in the area. Now situated within Lake Crabtree County Park, the reservoir offers sailing and various recreational opportunities for nearby residents, making it a cherished local resource.

properties.name: Buckhorn Disc Golf Course
properties.description:
Established in 2001, Buckhorn at Harris Lake Park, is considered the most challenging course in the area. With tight fairways, lots of out of bounds and water on six holes (including four throw overs,) this course will test your accuracy as well as distance.

properties.name: Lake Raleigh
properties.description:
Cut into the southern side of Centennial Campus and surrounded by a protected forest, Lake Raleigh offers a picturesque retreat from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Open to the public, this 75-acre lake features a fishing pier and boat ramp for non-motorized watercraft, such as kayaks and canoes. Fish in the lake include largemouth bass and catfish.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Pullen Park
properties.description: Established in 1887 and designated as the first public park in N.C., Pullen Park in Raleigh is the fifth oldest amusement park in the U.S. and the 16th oldest in the world. Nestled between downtown Raleigh and the main campus of North Carolina State University, Pullen Park is known for terrific recreational opportunities—especially for kids and families—the park includes an operating carousel built in 1911, a miniature train you can ride through the park, pedal boats to cruise around Lake Howell, plus tennis courts, baseball and softball fields, an arts center and an innovative performing arts venue, Theatre In The Park (Ira David Wood III Pullen Park Theatre). Free admission; small fee for amusement rides. Hours vary; call or visit website for more details.

properties.name: Cary Senior Center
properties.description:
Cary Senior Center is a more than 17,000-square-foot recreational and educationl facility in Cary, N.C. It is a meeting center for local senior citizens and holds recreational activities and exercise classes on a daily basis. The center operates Resources for Seniors, which is an information and referral service. Cary Senior Center also operates SeniorNet, which provides computer resources and training to seniors. The center features a courtyard gazebo, arts and crafts, ball, media, exercise and conference rooms.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Holding Park Aquatic Center
properties.description:
Holding Park Aquatic Center offers a six-lane, 25-yard lap pool, two water slides with plunge pool and children's pool with water play.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Joel Lane Museum House Gardens
properties.description:
Beautiful Neo-Colonial garden featuring espaliered fruit trees, pomegranate trees, a grape arbor and brick walkways. Herb garden features medicinal and culinary herbs. Free admission to garden only. Garden Hours: Daily, sunrise -sunset. Docent-guided tours, which include the historic home, discuss colonial uses of herbs and some modern-day applications. Cost: $5 for adults, $4 for seniors, $3 for students, free for children under 6. Tour Hours: Wed.-Fri., 10am-2pm; Sat., 1-4pm. Last tour begins one hour before closing.

Photo Credit
Photo Link

properties.name: John M. Brown Community Center
properties.description:
Located on the Apex Town Hall Campus, the Apex Community Center offers a variety of programs for all ages, from preschoolers to seniors. The center has several rooms available for rent. The three largest rooms are separated by partition walls that can open to accommodate the need for more than one room's capacity.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Juniper Level Botanic Garden
properties.description:
Established in 1988, JLBG is a 28-acre education, research and display garden with over 23,000 unique plants from around the world. JLBG is the private garden of Tony and Anita Avent. Open only eight weekends per year, two weekends each in winter, spring, summer and fall and at other times by scheduled weekday appointment only.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Laurel Hills Recreation Center
properties.description:
Laurel Hills Park and Recreational Center is a community hub in Raleigh, NC that offers a variety of recreational activities and amenities for visitors of all ages.

With a focus on promoting health and wellness, the center provides opportunities for exercise, socialization, and relaxation in a welcoming and inclusive environment.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Pullen Community Center
properties.description:
Pullen Park is a 66.4-acre (0.27 km2) public park immediately west of downtown Raleigh, North Carolina. It is located on Ashe Avenue and is adjacent to the Main and Centennial campuses of North Carolina State University, covering an area between Western Boulevard and historic Hillsborough Street. Founded in 1887, Pullen Park is the oldest public park in North Carolina.

The park features picnic areas, a concessions stand along with several small rides including the Pullen Park Carousel, train, and kiddie boats. Pedal boats are also available for rent seasonally on the park's small lake. The Pullen Aquatic Center, Pullen Arts Center and Theatre in the Park are also located on the park grounds. It is one of the most famous and well-known parks in the Research Triangle region.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Ridge Road Pool
properties.description:
Ridge Road Pool is a seasonal aquatic center that operates June 2-Sept. 3 each year and offers both a standard swimming pool with lap swimming, recreational swimming, wading area and splash pad. Located adjacent to Martin Middle School, Ridge Road Pool offers entry fees for both residents and non-residents.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Dorothea Dix Park
properties.description: Dorothea Dix Park is the site of one of the most exciting new park projects in America. The 308-acre Dorothea Dix Park, in the heart of downtown Raleigh, blends historic architecture with beautiful rolling hills, huge shade trees and stunning views of the Raleigh skyline. Dorothea Dix Park is open to the public daily from dawn to dusk. Visit dixpark.org for more details about events and programs at the park, as well as continued planning efforts.

properties.name: Pullen Park
properties.description: Established in 1887 and designated as the first public park in N.C., Pullen Park in Raleigh is the fifth oldest amusement park in the U.S. and the 16th oldest in the world. Nestled between downtown Raleigh and the main campus of North Carolina State University, Pullen Park is known for terrific recreational opportunities—especially for kids and families—the park includes an operating carousel built in 1911, a miniature train you can ride through the park, pedal boats to cruise around Lake Howell, plus tennis courts, baseball and softball fields, an arts center and an innovative performing arts venue, Theatre In The Park (Ira David Wood III Pullen Park Theatre). Free admission; small fee for amusement rides. Hours vary; call or visit website for more details.

properties.name: William B. Umstead State Park
properties.description: Stroll nature trails or walk along 22 miles of hiking trails meandering through forest. Also offered are camping, picnicking, canoe rentals, fishing, visitor center nature study and 13 miles of horseback-riding and mountain-biking trails. Free admission; fee for boat and facility rental. Hours: Daily, 8am-sunset approximately; call or visit website.

properties.name: Historic Yates Mill County Park
properties.description: The 174-acre wildlife park features hiking trails, Historic Yates Mill, Wake County’s last remaining gristmill, and the mill’s 24-acre pond, which is fed by Steep Hill Creek. The 18th century water-powered mill is fully restored and operable. Free admission to the park; mill tour fee: $3-5 (all proceeds directly support the mill's ongoing maintenance and operations). Park hours: Daily, 8am-sunset; Finley Center: Daily, 8:30am-5pm; mill tour hours are limited and vary seasonally.

properties.name: Downtown Cary Park
properties.description: Cary's Downtown Park is a jewel in the crown of the revitalization of Downtown Cary. A true urban park, the space anchors the corner of S. Academy St. and Kildaire Farm Rd., across from Cary Arts Center. The centerpiece of the park is a stunning, lighted fountain. Truly a community gathering place, the Downtown Park offers places for musical performances, outdoor movies, recreation, games, public art and simply enjoying the outdoors. Open daily, 7am-11pm.

properties.name: John Chavis Memorial Park and Community Center
properties.description: Named for early 19th-century free Black preacher and teacher of all races John Chavis (ca. 1762-1838), the 37-acre City of Raleigh park was opened as a recreational spot for the city’s Black residents during segregation. It was dedicated in 1938, and the circa-1923 carousel still can be ridden. Cost: $1.50 for carousel. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset (except carousel, Tues.-Wed. and Sun., 11am-6pm).

properties.name: Historic Oak View County Park
properties.description: This antebellum farmstead features an 1855 Greek Revival house, detached kitchen, cotton gin house, livestock barn, carriage house, pecan grove and herb garden. Enjoy picnic facilities and stop in the Farm History Center, where kids learn through play in the interactive “Farmer’s Corner.” Free admission. Hours: Mon.-Sat., 8:30am-5pm; Sun., 1-5pm.

properties.name: Lake Crabtree County Park
properties.description: Located on the shores of a 520-acre lake, the park offers hiking, single-track mountain biking and nature trails, seasonal boat rentals, two playgrounds, play fields, picnic facilities and environmental education programs. The park also offers fishing by boat and from a fishing pier (catch and release only) and platform for the physically challenged. Free admission. Hours: Daily, 8am-sunset.

properties.name: Blue Jay Point County Park
properties.description: Located on the shores of Falls Lake in northern Wake County, the 236-acre park's mission of environmental education is accomplished through exhibits, demonstration areas and educational programming. The park also offers picnicking, hiking trails, open play fields, playgrounds and a Go Ape TreeTop Adventure Course. Park admission is free and hours are 8am-sunset, daily.

properties.name: Garner Recreational Park
properties.description: Garner Recreational Park is located in the Historic Garner District. This park features two ball fields, a playground and 2.25 miles of mountain biking trails. In the Creech Rd. section of the park, at 190 Creech Rd., there are lighted tennis courts. Please call to reserve athletic fields.

properties.name: Lake Johnson Park
properties.description: Lake Johnson Park comprises more than 300 acres of land surrounding the 150-acre lake. The lake offers boat rentals (jonboats, paddleboats, canoes, kayaks, sailboats, SUPs) and personal boat launches (non-motorized, non-trailered boats). The park also boats picnic shelters, concessions, facility rentals and Capital Area Greenway access, as well as an array of classes and recreational opportunities for the entire family. The lake is great for fishing of largemouth bass, shell cracker, crappie, bream, catfish and carp. Free admission; fee for boat launches and facility rentals. Open daily, sunrise-sunset (closed Mon., Oct.-March).

properties.name: Anderson Point Park
properties.description: Anderson Point Park, opened in 1988, offers a variety of habitats for wildlife viewing and is home to the Anderson Family Homestead and Amphitheater.

properties.name: Shelley Lake Park
properties.description: This 53-acre lake and park provides two miles of paved, scenic greenway trails with exercise workout stations. Visitors may enjoy fishing, biking, hiking and picnicking. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: Green Hills County Park
properties.description: A day at North Wake Landfill District Park provides a variety of recreational activities for all ages. The park includes a playground, trail access, picnic shelter and restrooms facilities.

properties.name: North Carolina Freedom Park
properties.description:
Freedom Park is a one-acre green space nestled in the heart of downtown Raleigh, N.C. With deep reverence for the spirit of the African American struggle for freedom, this park stands as a timeless tribute to the universal ideals of liberty, resilience and equality.

Anchored by the Beacon of Freedom, the park features 20 "Voices of Freedom" inscribed along its walkways--powerful words of African Americans throughout North Carolina history. As the first park in N.C. dedicated to honoring the African American struggle for freedom, it stands as a beacon of hope and a reminder that the ideals of perseverance, equality and freedom are universal aspirations that can unite us all. Free admission. Hours: Daily, dawn-dusk.

properties.name: Carl Alwin Schenck Memorial Forest
properties.description: The Carl Alwin Schenck Memorial Forest is a 245 acre forest located in western Wake County about 10 minutes from the NC State campus. It is managed by N.C. State as a teaching and research forest to demonstrate the multiple benefits generated by an actively-managed forest. Visitors can walk the well-maintained trails to enjoy bird-watching and wildlife, see a managed forest that shows successional stages and enjoy the well-maintained picnic facilities. The Frances L. Liles Trail is most frequently used by the public. This trail passes through a number of sites where a variety of management practices are being employed, including those to support different wildlife habitats and encourage specific plants and animals.

properties.name: Prairie Ridge Ecostation
properties.description:
Prairie Ridge Ecostation was established by the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences for research and educational purposes. Visitors are welcome to walk the designated trails during the posted hours.

Prairie Ridge currently has two walking trails open to the public.

properties.name: Mill Bridge Nature Park
properties.description: Mill Bridge Nature Park has a 200-seat amphitheater along with greenway trails that currently connect with the Wake Forest Parks and Recreation greenways. The town has future plans to connect with the current greenway tails at Main Street Park.

properties.name: Veterans Park
properties.description: Veterans Park is dedicated to the men and women who have served our country in the military. The park features a liberty elm donated by the Elm Research Institute of Keene, N.H. as an enduring symbol of freedom. The park also includes a 4.3-acre pond, picnic shelter, playground, fitness stations, half-mile paved trail extending around the pond and a paved trail between Veterans Park and Jones Park.

properties.name: Centennial Park
properties.description: This beautiful park features soccer fields, picnic shelter and .36 miles of paved walking trails. The shelter is available for rental and can seat 50 people. Centennial Park is used as part of the CASL National Soccer Series program and is one of their 13 venues.

properties.name: Blue Lotus
properties.description: Our story is our mission: It is our intention to lovingly welcome you as you are, and to provide a space that nurtures and supports you on your journey. We are dedicated to creating true community, helping all of us to better connect with ourselves and those around us. In our urban sanctuary, we challenge each individual to be fully present, and invite you to uncover a new way of being in your body and the world. With open hearts, we receive everything we need. Join us.

properties.name: CYCLEBAR
properties.description:
CycleBar is not your average cycling class—it’s a mind-blowing, heart-pumping party on a bike. Every ride is led by an elite CycleStar Instructor, each with their own style and vibe. No two rides are alike; from the music to the intensity to the overall vibe, instructors keep it fresh and keep you motivated every single class.
When you ride with them, you ride in style in the CycleTheatre, a fully-loaded, epic cycling space. With high-performance custom bikes, amphitheater seating, enhanced lighting, concert-quality sound and two massive high-def flat screens, they set the scene for an immersive, exhilarating experience. Every bike comes with built-in CycleStats technology, so you can track calories burned, RPMs, watts and class rank. 
Whether you want to start your day strong or melt away the stress of the day, once the lights go down and the music goes up, you’ll leave the outside world behind.

properties.name: DefyGravity
properties.description: DefyGravity is a cutting-edge Trampoline Sports Arena unlike anything you have ever experienced. Part entertainment venue and part sports gym, DefyGravity is the ultimate destination for active social outings, memorable birthday parties, intense individual workouts, competitive team sports and creative fundraisers. DefyGravity is a 20,000-square-foot facility with wall-to-wall steel-frame trampolines including the world-famous Angled Wall Trampolines, an expansive Olympic Foam Pit and one of the largest Trampoline Dodgeball cages in America. Come play, relieve stress and turn on the adrenaline in a unique and exhilarating atmosphere. Visit website for complete list of hours and age exclusive jump times.

properties.name: Dose Yoga + Smoothie Bar
properties.description:
Yoga it-girl, Emily Wallace, brings a new way to sweat and refresh to Raleigh with DOSE Yoga Studio and Smoothie Bar.  At DOSE, we believe balance is bad ass and we are here to help you find yours. Down Dog to our Down Beats while our top notch instructors guide you through your practice.  Whether you want to strengthen your core, stretch past some stress, or sweat through a flow, you will leave class more energized and ready to refuel at the DOSE Elixir Bar.  At Raleigh’s first hot yoga studio and smoothie bar, pick your potion of real ingredients and natural adaptogens that will enhance your mood, adapt to stress, and keep you balanced.

Come in and get your Daily DOSE. Positive Side Effects Guaranteed.

properties.name: Ellen Mordecai Garden
properties.description: The garden is recreated from first-hand descriptions of the Mordecai kitchen garden in the 1830s. It contains vegetables, herbs and flowers that were grown through the 19th century and is arranged in squares of raised beds. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: Greystone Recreation Center
properties.description:
The first of its kind indoor recreation center, is 9,600 square-feet and features an indoor play area, a rock climbing wall, a dance/fitness studio along with meeting rooms and classrooms. The center is open Monday through Friday from 9am-7pm and Saturday from 9am-3pm. This is the first time the city has placed a recreation center in a shopping center. The vision for this space was to offer a wide variety of recreational programs for the neighboring community. The center features indoor playground elements, a dance/fitness studio and two classrooms. The center offers a wide variety of opportunities in the education, fitness arts and social programs geared towards meeting the needs of the community. Classes and activities are offered year-round and are flexible depending on interests. A sample of offerings may include Yoga or Tai Chi, Beginner Tap or Ballroom Dance, Photography or Drawing, First Aid or Basic Spanish.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Go Ape Treetop Adventure & Treetop Journey
properties.description:
Zip, swing and climb through the trees! Go Ape's Treetop Adventure course is a highly interactive 2-3 hour outdoor aerial high ropes experience featuring 5 zip lines, 2 Tarzan swings and awesome obstacles at heights of 40-50 feet in the trees. Treetop Journey is a one-hour adventure for all ages, featuring 20 obstacles and 2 zip lines at a height of 20 feet in the trees. Go Ape is a great outdoor adventure for families, friends and groups.

Treetop Adventure is open seasonally, March 2-Nov. 30 each year.  Treetop Journey operates March 16-Nov. 30.

Photo credit: Go Ape.

properties.name: Garner Senior Center
properties.description:
Garner was very proud to help meet the needs and desire of its senior population when it constructed the Garner Senior Center in 1990. This multipurpose, 6,800-sq.-ft. facility serves as a focal point for senior/adult programs and activities.With its overwhelming growth to over 2,500 registered participants, the need for a new addition was determined, and in 2006, a half-court gymnasium, restrooms, changing rooms, an exercise room, a catering kitchen, storage area and office space were built as part of this facility. Senior and adult activities can now include indoor sports, yoga, exercise classes and events that were unable to be offered before due to space limitations.The renovated Senior Center continues to serve the community well as it provides additional recreation and cultural arts activities for adults and seniors. The facility is available for rental by non-tax-exempt groups or individuals for activities such as reunions, birthday parties, baby showers, church functions and weddings. It is reserved on a first-come, first-served basis for public and private events.The space is available weekends and some evenings. Groups and individuals may reserve the facilities by contacting the Garner Senior Center. Reservations are accepted 90 days prior to the event.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: Haywood Hall House and Gardens
properties.description: John Haywood, the state’s first elected treasurer, built this Federal-style frame house in 1799. It is the oldest house on its original site within the city limits of Raleigh. The house museum contains family portraits, original furnishings and a permanent doll collection. Free admission; donations accepted. Hours: 2nd and 4th Thurs., 11am-3pm (Mar.-Nov.)

properties.name: Midtown Yoga
properties.description: Midtown Yoga's mission is to inspire, challenge, and celebrate the perfectly imperfect you. Your life, your journey, your purpose. Through a holistic and mindful yoga experience, we strive to nourish the mind, body and soul.

properties.name: North Carolina Esports Academy
properties.description:
North Carolinae Esports Academy in Cary, NC offers a fun, innovative, and educational approach to the gaming world. Our location serves as the premier Educational Video Gaming Center for the Raleigh, N.C. area.

North Carolina Esports Academy was opened in October 2020 by Caleb Smith (a lifelong gamer and athlete) and Vinny Smith (computer programmer). North Carolina Esports Academy is dedicated to building character and life skill development through productive video gaming. Caleb, Vinny, and the entire staff are committed to creating premier youth development experiences in order to create pathways for youth in STEM careers.

properties.name: OnPoint Range
properties.description: OnPoint makes the sport of shooting seriously fun, easy to learn and safe for everyone. Not only are we one of the most technologically advanced ranges in the world, we’re focused on ensuring a truly unique and exciting range experience for you and your guests. With our 25-yard main bay and two 15-yard group bays, we’ve got exciting options whether you want to plan something with a few friends or need to coordinate a big group event. Looking for a more inclusive experience? Reserve our conference room, a private bay, and pick one of our event packages with options like firearm rentals and pop-up targets. Our friendly OnPoint staff can’t wait to work with you to provide a memorable experience.

properties.name: Peach Road Cultural Center
properties.description: Located in South East Raleigh, Peach Rd Community Center is only 3 miles from Downtown. Opened in 2004 Peach Rd has 2 multi-use rooms and a fully equipped kitchen. Outside we have a tot lot, basketball courts, a multi-purpose field and a handball court. It’s perfect for family reunions, kids’ birthdays, Employee trainings and church rentals.

properties.name: Raleigh Municipal Rose Garden
properties.description: An historic garden featuring 1,200 roses of 60 different varieties blooming from late May until autumn. Seasonal flowers include bulbs, annuals, trees and shrubs. An amphitheatre for concerts and theatrical productions is also located in the garden. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: The Albatross
properties.description: Located in downtown Cary, N.C., The Albatross offers a unique experience for everyone. From state-of-the-art golf simulators to a carefully curated menu of gourmet hotdogs, smash burgers and beverages, The Albatross lets you eat, drink and play like the pros.

properties.name: The Well Fed Community Garden
properties.description: The Well Fed Community Garden hosts many opportunities to connect folks of all ages with how food is grown – Volunteering, Workshops, Farm Dinners and more – Bringing Community to the Table with Healing Models for Living. Everyone is welcome to ‘Enter the Garden’!

properties.name: Rebel Moves Pilates
properties.description:
Rebel Moves Pilates is your path to improved overall health, joint mobility, balance, and endurance. Pilates is a unique low and no impact form of exercise using your body weight and resistance to create healthy movement patterns, flexibility, and a powerful core. Widely recognized in the medical community as a successful form of alternative rehabilitation, Pilates offers recovery and convalescence support after surgery, injury and medical treatment. Pilates has proven to be very effective in maintaining and regaining quality of life while managing chronic conditions such as Arthritis, Osteoporosis, MS and Fibromyalgia. But many of our clients love Rebel Moves Pilates for the Classic Pilates we offer as a safe and impactful workout. Regardless of your age or condition, Pilates is good for you! We have exceptionally skilled and experienced instructors and state-of-the-art equipment producing a fresh experience with each visit. Choose from exclusively small classes creating a positive movement experience every time or private sessions with customized focus on your goals and requirements.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: TreeRunner Adventure Park
properties.description:
Discover a thrilling ziplining and climbing adventure at TreeRunner Adventure Park in Raleigh, North Carolina! This exhilarating outdoor park offers over 90 aerial obstacles, 20 ziplines and 13 unique courses, catering to all ages and skill levels, including a Junior Park specially designed for kids ages 4-7. From ziplines and swinging bridges to Tarzan swings and balance beams, you're guaranteed to find excitement and challenge at every turn.

Nestled in a beautiful forest setting, and open 10 months out of the year, TreeRunner Raleigh provides the perfect opportunity to connect with nature while testing your physical and mental agility. Our friendly and experienced staff is always on hand to ensure your safety and help guide you through the courses. 

Whether you're planning a family outing, birthday party, team-building event, or simply seeking a new adventure, TreeRunner Adventure Park in Raleigh promises a fun-filled day for everyone aged 4 and up. Book your tickets now at TreeRunnerParks.com/Raleigh and embark on an unforgettable journey through the trees!

Spring hours are Feb. 18-June 9. Summer hours are June 10-Aug. 27. Fall hours are Aug. 28-Dec. 18

properties.name: WRAL Azalea Gardens
properties.description:
Imagine yourself on a breezy spring day basking in the warm rays of the sun, surrounded by beautiful azaleas of all shapes and colors. Wonderful fragrances fill the air, providing another dimension of delight for your senses. You're thousands of miles from anywhere...

All of this is yours and it's closer than you think at the WRAL Azalea Gardens in Raleigh, N.C. Situated conveniently behind the WRAL-TV 5 television studios, the Azalea Gardens offer tranquility and beauty beyond measure.

properties.name: Wake Forest Yoga Studio
properties.description: Wake Forest Yoga Studio's mission is to bring yoga to everybody who wants to live a healthier and happier life. Our classes are inclusive and available to all. We teach in a respectful way honoring yoga’s historical foundations.

properties.name: Zin Yoga & Wine
properties.description:
Zin Yoga Studio and Wine Lounge, located in Garner, N.C., was created with the intention of fostering community through both yoga and wine. Our two passions and businesses operate separately under one roof, and although there will be no drinking at the top of the mat, you are more than welcome to stay for a glass after class!

What matters most to us is that our space is one where genuinely and truly ALL are welcome; where folks of all shapes, colors, sizes, backgrounds, experiences and beliefs can come together to care for and connect more deeply with self and community. Our vision is that of a watering hole – a place where ALL can come, regardless of our differences, to receive the nourishment we need.

Our tribe is everything and we hope you’ll join us as we skip, stumble, laugh, love, breathe and sip our way along. We have everything from group classes to one-on-one instruction, public wine tastings with local food trucks, live music events and concerts, private wine parties, luxury retreats to yoga teacher trainings, and SO much more.

properties.name: Cary Dog Park at Godbold Park
properties.description:
Located in Robert V. Godbold Park, Cary Dog Park offers a place to let dogs run safely and legally without a leash. The one acre park features a five-foot high fence, wood chip ground cover, water bowls, pet clean up stations, and lights for evening use. Day Pass or annual membership is required.

Photo Credit:
Photo Link

properties.name: JC Raulston Arboretum at North Carolina State University
properties.description:
The JC Raulston Arboretum is a nationally acclaimed garden with one of the largest and most diverse collections of landscape plants adapted for landscape use in the southeastern U.S. Plant collections include nearly 6,000 total taxa (unique taxonomic groups) of annuals, perennials, bulbs, vines, ground covers, shrubs, and trees from over 50 different countries, which are displayed in a beautiful garden setting. The JC Raulston Arboretum is also a public garden, and it is open most every day of the year. The Arboretum provides a pleasant garden environment and a unique experience for groups seeking a special location to schedule their staff and client conferences, workshops, board meetings, etc. The highly aesthetic sustainable landscape is a favorite location for many university and public groups to conduct their meetings.


The York Auditorium in the Ruby McSwain Education Center offers a space that can accommodate 100-150 people with tables and chairs or 200 people with chairs only or can be divided into three sound-proof rooms, each section with a capacity of 30 to 50 people depending upon the section and set-up needs. Various set-up arrangements are selected by each group and set-ups are completed by JCRA undergraduate student facilitators.


The JC Raulston Arboretum also has more than 10 garden spaces that can be reserved for events. For example, there are approximately 25 weddings held in the Klein-Pringle White Garden and gazebo each year. Want a spectacular view? Schedule your event on our Rooftop Terrace. The panoramic view and outstanding selection of plants, high above the Ruby C. McSwain Education Center on the A. E. Finley Foundation rooftop terrace is a great place to schedule a theater presentation or other creative events. This dramatic green roof is an integral part of the building and environment, and it provides an insulating factor for the geothermally heated and cooled McSwain Center. Need a large space for an outdoor garden party? The JCRA has one, and each year the signature Gala in the Garden hosts more than 500 guests. It is a wide open space surrounded by the lovely gardens that is perfect for most any special occasion or event.

properties.name: Carolina Pines Dog Park
properties.description:
Raleigh’s newest dog park contains three fenced
dog areas, including one for training, each covered
in a layer of mulch.
Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: Cary Dog Park at Jack Smith Park
properties.description: Located in Jack Smith Park, Cary Dog Park offers a place to let dogs run safely and legally without a leash.  The one acre park features a five-foot high fence, wood chip ground cover, water bowls, pet clean up stations, and lights for evening use.  Day Pass or annual membership is required.

properties.name: Dix Park Dog Park
properties.description:
The Dix Park Dog Park provides a much needed off-leash dog area for park visitors, with all other areas of Dix Park requiring dogs to be on-leash. The 4-acre dog park is open to the public seven days a week from sunrise to sunset and includes separate areas for small and large dogs. To ensure that the field and fencing remains in good condition Dix Park Dog Park will close the last week of each month for routine maintenance.
Know Before You Go:

Dogs are required to be on-leash in all other areas of Dix Park.
Be sure to bring a water bottle for yourself and your furry friends, too.
There are no public restrooms at the park, only port-a-johns.
North Carolina DHHS administrative headquarters are located on park grounds.
Please be respectful of the employees at work and avoid the buildings and parking areas during business hours.

properties.name: Fuquay-Varina Downtown Dog Park
properties.description: The Fuquay-Varina Downtown Dog Park is an 8-acre, off-leash dog park with free admission.  The park is split into a large breed area (30 pounds and up) and small breed area (under 30 pounds). Sanitary stations, benches and water stations are available as well as lots of shade and play for your furry friends. Please close gates.

properties.name: Millbrook Dog Park
properties.description:
Raleigh’s oldest dog park and only dog park with
lights, it features a large dog area and small dog area.
Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-10pm approximately.

properties.name: North Hills Dog Park
properties.description: The North Hills Dog Park is located in the Park District at North Hills. The 9,500-square-foot dog park is an off-leash dog park and open to the public.

properties.name: Oakwood Dog Park
properties.description:
Oakwood features a large dog area as well as a small dog area for older dogs or those that are anxious around larger dogs.
Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: The Ashley Wilder Dog Park
properties.description: Knightdale Station is a 76-acre park in eastern Wake County. The Ashley Wilder Dog Park features fields for active recreation, a destination playground, multi-purpose trails, scout camping site and an off-leash dog park, divided into two sections for small and large breeds. Open daily from dawn until dusk.

properties.name: North Carolina State Capitol
properties.description: Completed in 1840, this National Historic Landmark is one of the best-preserved examples of a civic building in Greek Revival-style architecture. It originally housed the governor's office, cabinet offices, legislative chambers, state library and state geologist's office.

properties.name: North Carolina Museum of Art
properties.description:
The North Carolina Museum of Art has more than a dozen galleries holding works from around the world and a variety of art types. Originally starting with 139 works from Europe and America, the museum has grown to include African, Egyptian and Jewish works of art while also expanding European and ancient American holdings. With 30 added Rodin sculptures, the NCMA leads the holdings of this artist’s work in the southeastern United States. Other galleries hold everything from Renaissance paintings to contemporary photography. Exhibitions also run at the museum for several months at a time for guests to visit.


Outside the museum is the 164-acre Ann and Jim Goodnight Museum Park, recently expanded and featuring monumental public art installations inspired by the natural world and preservation of landscapes, including the Gyre rings, Cloud Chamber for the Trees and Sky and Askew, as well as several recreational activities, picnic spots and wooded trails.


Tours are given daily if you or a group would like to learn more about the collections.


When it’s time for lunch, you can stop by the Iris restaurant located inside the museum, specializing in contemporary American cuisine in a modern setting. (Also open for dinner! Order from items such as the Iris Burger, Seared Scallops with Red Curry Lemongrass Broth, Seafood Burrito and more.)


For those interested in researching art periods or artists, the Art Reference Library holds over 40,000 volumes of books and available catalogues and databases. Kids to seniors can enjoy the many programs occurring throughout the year, including classes, concerts, films, camps and workshops.


Before you leave, head by the Museum Store, where items based on the museum’s collections and exhibits are available to purchase, perfect as souvenirs or gifts for family and friends. Admission is free, while some fees are given for specific programs, exhibitions and large tours. Hours: Wed.-Sun., 10am-5pm; Mon., closed.; Tues., closed.

properties.name: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
properties.description:
The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences is the Southeast’s largest natural history museum, complete with its Nature Exploration Center and Nature Research Center, with four floors of exhibits, live animals, gift shops and cafés. Explore on a variety of different self-guided tours through all the different exhibits.


In the Nature Exploration Center, you can view more than a dozen exhibits from coastal to prehistoric North Carolina, see a live sloth in the Living Conservatory, engage in hands-on activities in the Discovery Room and experience life as a bug in the Arthropod Zoo. Here, you can also visit the world’s most complete Acrocanthosaurus dinosaur, the “Terror of the South.”


Head to the Nature Research Center where you can get a glimpse of a different side of natural science with labs, weather centers and ocean, fossils and space exhibits plus a 10,000-gallon aquarium. Living collections include fish, butterflies, reptiles and amphibians. This museum wing’s centerpiece is the SECU Daily Planet, a 70-foot-diameter globe with a three-story theater for live programming and movies on its giant screen. Snap some great photos of the exterior--one of Raleigh’s most popular spots for Instagrams!


The museum also includes vast amounts of resources for hands-on learning and research. Educators and workshops are available for schools and other groups. Outreach and e-learning programs are sponsored for all ages. The Brimley Memorial Library is open in the Nature Exploration Center, with the archives of the museum in circulation. Online collections are accessible in the museum’s database.


On your trip to Raleigh, N.C., you won’t want to miss out on this incredible, world-class museum, an affiliate of the Smithsonian Institution. Visit the museum in downtown Raleigh and see why it’s one of the top places to visit in Raleigh and the state! Hours: Tue.-Sun., 10am-5pm. Closed on Mondays. Free general admission.

properties.name: Art to Heart Corridor/Art to Heart Trail
properties.description: Beginning at the North Carolina Museum of Art (where parking and admission to the museum are free) and ending in downtown Raleigh, this 5.9-mile paved trail winds through the museum’s beautiful 164-acre park, passes behind Meredith College, cuts through the main campus at North Carolina State University, zips by Pullen Park and finishes in the heart of the city just outside of the Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts.

properties.name: Andrew Johnson Birthplace
properties.description: President of the United States, 1865-69; led U.S. through reconstruction after Civil War; born 64 yards west of marker.

properties.name: Anna J. Cooper Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: Anna Julia Haywood Cooper (1858-1964) is remembered as an educator, orator and early Black feminist. She was born into slavery but, after gaining freedom, began attending Saint Augustine's University in 1868. After graduating there, Cooper earned additional degrees from Oberlin College in Ohio and Paris’s Sorbonne. Her distinguished career in higher education and her book “A Voice from the South” have caused Dr. Cooper to be quoted on the U.S. passport and depicted on a 2009 U.S. postage stamp.

properties.name: Artificial Limbs
properties.description: North Carolina was first state to provide artificial limbs to Confederate amputees; factory was 1/4 mi NE.

properties.name: Berry O’Kelly Training School Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: Founded in 1910 and located in the Method community, a 69-acre, Reconstruction-era village started by freedmen Jesse Mason and Isaac O’Kelly. The boarding school was among the first rural high schools for Blacks in North Carolina, providing its students with a sound education and the entire community with new carpenters, laundresses, seamstresses and teachers. Berry O’Kelly (1861-1931) was a Raleigh business leader. The school closed in 1966, and all but two of its buildings were demolished in 1969.

properties.name: Black Main Street
properties.description: From Fayetteville St. to Moore Square, E. Hargett St. developed as a commercial district and the Black main street of downtown Raleigh in the 1910s and 1920s. Its brick buildings housed the offices of Black doctors, lawyers, pharmacists and real estate developers as well as barbershops and retailers. The heart of the street was the 1921 Lightner Arcade, and another anchor was the Mechanics and Farmers Bank, an institution that remains today as M&F Bank.

properties.name: Borden Building
properties.description: The Borden Building is one of two remaining buildings on the former campus of the Methodist Home for Children. Built in 1900, it was home to the superintendent of the orphanage and later served as home to hundreds of children. Purchased by the City of Raleigh in 1982, the house and its companion, Fred Fletcher Park, provides a wealth of history and tranquility in an urban setting. The Borden Building was extensively renovated in 1992 and is presently available for weddings, receptions, meetings and small conferences.

properties.name: Burke Square
properties.description: The commissioners originally recommended Burke Square Park as "a suitable place for the Governor's House," but this recommendation was not followed. Between 1797 and 1883, the Governor had three different residences in various locations in the city. In 1883, after aggressive lobbying by Governor Thomas J. Jarvis, the governor's mansion was constructed in Burke Square Park, where it remains to this day. Local Confederate training ground during the Civil War.

properties.name: Camp Mangum
properties.description: Thousands of Confederate troops trained at Camp Mangum, which encompassed the grounds now occupied by the state fairgrounds, N.C. State University Faculty Club, School of Veterinary Science and the N.C. Museum of Art.

properties.name: Charles N. Hunter Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: Black teacher, journalist and reformer who lived from 1852 to 1931. Born into slavery, he witnessed changes in race relations from emancipation to Reconstruction to segregation and drew upon these varied experiences in his life’s work. Hunter was a founder of the North Carolina Industrial Association, host of an annual state fair, which became the most popular social event for Blacks statewide. From 1910 to 1918, he served as principal of the Berry O’Kelly Training School in Raleigh.

properties.name: City Cemetery
properties.description: Originally established in 1798 and divided into four parts: two one-acre plots for citizens, one for visitors and one for Blacks (mainly slaves); now covering seven acres. Its iron fence once surrounded the North Carolina State Capitol grounds to keep out straying livestock. Among the buried is Dr. Anna J. Cooper (1858-1964), publisher of “A Voice from the South.”

properties.name: College Park and Idlewild Neighborhoods
properties.description: The neighborhoods of College Park and Idlewild surround the Saint Augustine's University campus, which itself is a National Register Historic District. These historically Black neighborhoods—College Park to the east of Tarboro St. and Idlewild to the west—feature many well-maintained vernacular houses, not to mention the Gothic and Romanesque buildings at Saint Augustine's itself.

properties.name: Davie St. Presbyterian Church
properties.description: Originally a mission to teach freed Black children and send them to schools of higher education, the initial congregation occupied a building on this site in 1875. The present church was remodeled and enlarged in the 1920s by Calvin Lightner, a church elder for 62 years. The building is distinguished by its Gothic details, tower and slate roof.

properties.name: Dorothea Dix Hospital
properties.description:
Dorothea Dix Hospital was authorized in 1849 and named for Dorothea L. Dix, crusader for better care for the mentally ill. The hospital grounds at one time included 2,354 acres, which were used for the hospital's farms, orchards, livestock, maintenance buildings, employee housing, and park grounds. 

Union troops camped on Dix Hill in April 1865 as part of Sherman’s March to the Sea. In 1984, the Hunt administration transferred 385 acres to NC State University. In 2012, Dorothea Dix Hospital moved its last patients and formally closed the hospital. In 2015, the remaining 308-acres of the original Dorothea Dix Hospital property was transferred to the City of Raleigh and become Dorothea Dix Park.

properties.name: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Gardens
properties.description: The first public park in the United States solely devoted to Dr. King and the civil rights movement, it is bordered by the King Memorial Wall of 2,500 named bricks recognizing state and national supporters of the facility. A colorful variety of trees, shrubs and flowering plants encircle a life-sized bronze statue of King, and a 12-ton granite water monument honors the area’s notable pioneers in the civil rights movement. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: Edward A. Johnson Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: Born into slavery but educated in Raleigh then Atlanta, Edward Johnson (1860-1944) returned to be principal at the Washington Graded and High School from 1885 to 1891. While there, he was the first Black author to publish a North Carolina textbook; he also completed a law degree at Shaw University. Dr. Johnson’s highly successful career included working as a dean at Shaw, serving twice as a Republican National Convention delegate, practicing law in Harlem and being elected as a New York state legislator.

properties.name: Estey Hall
properties.description: Built in 1874, Estey Hall is the nation’s first dormitory for women on a co-educational campus and is Shaw University’s oldest surviving building. It was named for benefactor Jacob Estey and Company of Vermont. Bricks for the construction were handmade on the grounds of the university. Women first attended classes here in home economics, music, art and religion. Estey Hall remained a women’s dorm until 1968 and was closed in 1970. It was reopened in recent years as office space. Hours: Mon.-Fri., 9am-4pm.

properties.name: Fall of Raleigh
properties.description: Former governors William A. Graham and David L. Swain met officers of Sherman's army near this spot, on April 13, 1865, and surrendered the city, saving it from destruction.

properties.name: First Baptist Church
properties.description: Black members of the First Baptist Church on N. Salisbury St., established in 1812 as a multiracial congregation, requested separation in 1868 to form their own church and acquired the present lot across from the North Carolina State Capitol in the 1870s. The present 1904 church is a brick, gable-roofed building dominated by a square, brick tower and topped by a Gothic spire.

properties.name: Former J.W. Ligon High School
properties.description: Ligon Gifted and Talented Magnet Middle School has a heritage dating to its beginnings in 1953 as an historically Black high school. In 1971 the school was integrated as a junior high school and, in 1982, took on its current status as a magnet middle school in the consolidated Wake County Public School System. Ligon is now a National Magnet School of Excellence.

properties.name: Former Latta University
properties.description: An historically Black college founded by Rev. M.L. Latta in 1892 on his farm adjacent to Oberlin. Rev. Latta established the university to solve racial problems through the non-sectarian education of its students. His 1903 autobiography “The History of My Life and Work” can be read online. The university ceased operation around 1920, and its last remaining building, Latta House, burned in 2007.

properties.name: Former Lightner Arcade
properties.description: Built in 1921 by Shaw alumnus, builder and businessman Calvin E. Lightner (1877-1960), the arcade was the heart of downtown Raleigh’s Black main street and a hub for social life during segregation. The building housed a barber college and shop, drugstore, hotel, newspaper and restaurant. The hotel itself was one of few places for Black travelers to lodge between Florida and Washington, D.C., and it welcomed the period’s notables such as Count Basie and Duke Ellington. The arcade burned in 1970.

properties.name: Former Murphey School
properties.description: Located adjacent to downtown Raleigh’s Historic Oakwood district, this 1916 school building has been adapted for use as apartments for seniors and its attached auditorium for use as a performing arts theatre. As a public school, it was the testing ground for desegregation of the Raleigh school system in 1961, when William “Bill” Campbell, mayor of Atlanta from 1994 to 2002, began the second grade here. Murphey School was integrated peacefully, and integration of the rest of the system soon followed.

properties.name: Former Washington High School
properties.description: Washington Gifted and Talented Magnet Elementary School’s history starts with its completion in 1924 as the first public high school for Black students in Raleigh. The impressive Jacobean Revival-style structure is a reminder of 1920s public policy aimed at improving public education for Blacks as well as whites in North Carolina. Washington is now nationally recognized as a Magnet School of Distinction.

properties.name: Freedmen’s Convention Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: In the months following the Civil War, freed slaves held meetings throughout eastern North Carolina, which led to a statewide convention in Raleigh, Sept. 29-Oct. 3, 1865. Meeting at the site of present-day Saint Paul African Methodist Episcopal Church, 106 delegates from 34 of the state’s then-89 counties resolved to seek freedmen’s equal rights with whites, especially serving on juries, acting as their own counsel and voting in elections.

properties.name: Friendship School High School
properties.description: Of 20+ Rosenwald schools built in Wake County prior to 1932, only five, including this school, are visible today. Called a national treasure, these now-aging school buildings once served Black children throughout the segregated, rural South. Friendship School, receiving a grant from Rosenwald circa 1923-1924, was of the two-teacher type: it operated into the early 1950s. It was then completely remodeled to serve as a private residence. View from street; not open to the public.

properties.name: Gallery C
properties.description: One of the Southeast's pre-eminent fine art galleries, Gallery C is an elegant and open space located in the historic Russ-Edwards House (c. 1901). The gallery has been instrumental in N.C.'s art scene, featuring contemporary artists as well as historically important North Carolinian art, Haitian art, folk art, animation and antique prints.  Merely blocks away from the Governor's mansion, the Capital and museums, Gallery C is part of the heart of downtown Raleigh.

properties.name: Garner Veterans Memorial
properties.description: The Garner Veterans Memorial features pillars with the names of 67 Garner-area veterans who have died serving their country as well as historical narrative about the wars and conflicts in which the nation has been involved.

properties.name: General Grant
properties.description: In the Governor's Palace April 24-27, 1865, Grant conferred with Sherman and approved new terms for surrender of Johnston's Confederate Army.

properties.name: Governor Morehead School Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: The Governor Morehead School, North Carolina’s school for the blind, opened in 1845 as the N.C. Institution for the Education of the Deaf and Dumb and the Blind. In 1869, a branch of the school was established for visually or aurally challenged African Americans, located first on S. Bloodworth St. then relocated here in 1929. It was the nation’s first institute for Black blind students. Black and white blind students were integrated at the modern Governor Morehead School campus on Ashe Ave. by 1971.

properties.name: Heck-Andrews House
properties.description: Along historic Blount St. is one of the city’s clearest and most well-defined examples of the Second Empire architectural style: the Heck Andrews House. Across the street from the lieutenant governor’s office and just steps away from the governor’s mansion, the Heck Andrews House was completed in 1872 and occupied until the late 1980s. Now fully restored, the Heck Andrews House is the Raleigh office for N.C. Realtors®.

properties.name: Historic Boylan Heights
properties.description: The Boylan Heights neighborhood is one of Raleigh’s first planned suburbs. In design and architecture, it exemplifies middle class ideals of the early 1900s. Economic expansion in early 20th-century Raleigh resulted in an acute housing shortage. In response, real estate developers began purchasing portions of the old plantation lands ringing the city, where wooded lots, attractive architecture and restrictive covenants might attract would-be homeowners.

properties.name: Historic Oak View County Park
properties.description: This antebellum farmstead features an 1855 Greek Revival house, detached kitchen, cotton gin house, livestock barn, carriage house, pecan grove and herb garden. Enjoy picnic facilities and stop in the Farm History Center, where kids learn through play in the interactive “Farmer’s Corner.” Free admission. Hours: Mon.-Sat., 8:30am-5pm; Sun., 1-5pm.

properties.name: Historic Oakwood
properties.description: An historic neighborhood of lovingly-restored Victorian and early 20th-century homes in a great variety of styles and sizes, many with beautiful gardens. This 30-block area to the east of the 100-700 blocks of Person St. may be enjoyed by driving or walking; self-guided walking tour brochures available at the Raleigh, N.C., Visitor Information Center (off City Plaza, Fayetteville St., downtown Raleigh). Annual Garden Tour and Tea each May and Candlelight Tour each Dec. offer opportunities to enter homes and gardens.

properties.name: Historic Oakwood Cemetery
properties.description: Adjacent to Historic Oakwood, Oakwood Cemetery, with over 20,000 interments, is the resting place of approximately 1,500 Confederate soldiers, five Civil War generals, seven governors and numerous U.S. Senators. Established in 1869, it is an excellent example of Victorian landscaping and mortuary art. Download the mobile phone app by searching "Historic Oakwood" in your mobile store. Free admission. Hours: Daily, 8am-6pm (except winter, 8am-5pm).

properties.name: James H. Harris Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: James H. Harris (1832-1891) was freed from slavery in 1848, was apprenticed to a carpenter and later opened his own business in Raleigh. After attending Oberlin College and traveling abroad, Harris returned to Raleigh, attending the state’s 1865 Freedmen’s Convention and later constitutional convention. He was a founder of North Carolina’s Republican Party and was elected a state legislator. Harris is remembered as a local, state and national leader in Reconstruction politics: he is buried at Mount Hope Cemetery.

properties.name: James H. Young Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: Born near Henderson, N.C., just before the Civil War, James H. Young (1860-1921) was educated at Shaw University then hired to work in internal revenue collection. Young became involved in Republican Party politics, then other government and political work followed, including service in the state legislature. Young was owner and editor of the “Raleigh Gazette,” the principal voice of Black politics in the state from 1893 to 1898, and later colonel of a Black regiment organized for the Spanish-American War.

properties.name: Joel Lane Museum House
properties.description: Built in 1769, this landmark is Wake County’s oldest home. It became the “Birthplace of N.C.’s Capital” when Joel Lane sold 1,000 acres to the state in 1792 for the new capital. The site includes two other historic buildings and a museum store. Tours are provided by costumed docents. Admission and hours vary.

properties.name: John Chavis Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: John Chavis (ca. 1762-1838) was a prominent free Black preacher and educator who settled in Raleigh around 1810 and taught children of all races from his home, near present-day Chavis Memorial Park. Chavis had fought in the Revolutionary War at the age of 16 then had gone on to study at what are now Washington & Lee and Princeton universities; he had likely the best education of any African American of his day in North Carolina. Many of his students would later become state government leaders.

properties.name: John Chavis Memorial Park and Community Center
