properties.description: Named for early 19th-century free Black preacher and teacher of all races John Chavis (ca. 1762-1838), the 37-acre City of Raleigh park was opened as a recreational spot for the city’s African American residents during segregation. It was dedicated in 1938, and the circa-1923 carousel still can be ridden. After undergoing a multimillion dollar renovation the park reopened in 2021 and now also includes an updated community center, fitness room, gym, playground and interactive water feature.

properties.name: Knightdale Veterans Memorial
properties.description: The Knightdale Veterans Memorial is home to the Knightdale Blue Star and a Gold Star Memorials, honoring those who have served and died for our country and their families, and located in the heart of Knightdale Station Park.

properties.name: Kristin S. Conrad Lace Center & Raleigh Lace Museum
properties.description: Kristin S. Conrad Lace Center & Raleigh Lace Museum currently exhibits 400 years of lace and lacemaking. Stunning intricate lace pieces are displayed on walls and on tables. The museum offers self guided tours in four languages and features lacemakers on several days per month. A gift store is available with memorable hand-made lace works.

properties.name: L. O'B. Branch
properties.description: Location of home site of Lawrence O’Bryan Branch; Confederate brigadier general; president of Raleigh and Gaston Railroad, member of Congress 1855-1861; grave site 2/3 mi. east.

properties.name: L.L. Polk House
properties.description: Described as “gingerbread gothic,” this 1890 Victorian was built by Col. L.L. Polk, one of N.C.’s most prominent citizens. He was part-owner/publisher of Raleigh’s News and Observer, founder/editor of The Progressive Farmer, legislator, N.C.’s first Department of Agriculture commissioner and a leading founder of N.C. State University. Tours by appointment only.

properties.name: Leonard Medical Building
properties.description: Located at Shaw University, Leonard Medical School was the fifth African-American medical school but the first to offer a four-year curriculum. Founded in 1881 and named for benefactor Judson Wade Leonard, brother-in-law to Shaw’s founder Dr. Henry Martin Tupper, the school closed in 1918, having trained 400 Black physicians, most of whom went on to serve patients in the rural South. The school’s 25-bed hospital operated from 1885 to 1914. Hours: by appointment only.

properties.name: Marbles Kids Museum
properties.description:
Know Before You Go: Marbles is transforming the central courtyard into the Marbles Playway! Construction is expected to last until Oct. 2024.

For more information about navigating around Marbles during this time, click here.

Delivering purposeful play in a big way, Marbles allows children to imagine, discover and learn with two floors of interactive exhibits, birthday parties, special events and giant-screen IMAX films. Kids connect, communicate, create and learn through extraordinary adventures in play. For children ages one to 11, and adults. Admission starts at $9, children under one and members play free. Purchasing admission online before your visit is highly recommended.

properties.name: Memorial Belltower (North Carolina State University)
properties.description: Completed in 1937, the Memorial Belltower at North Carolina State University stands at the Hillsborough St. entrance to the main campus. The landmark is lighted for holidays that honor our veterans, such as Memorial Day and Veterans' Day, and to celebrate NC State's proudest occasions and achievements.

properties.name: Method Community
properties.description: A 69-acre village started in 1872 by freedmen Jesse Mason and Isaac O’Kelly, who sold its subdivided tracts as an alternative to more expensive housing offered to Blacks in Raleigh proper. The village originally was called Masonville and Slab Town until being named Method by the Norfolk and Southern Railroad in 1890. In addition to handsome vernacular houses, the community boasted the Berry O’Kelly Training School and Saint James A.M.E. Church. Method also had a post office until 1973.

properties.name: Mordecai Historic Park
properties.description: The Mordecai House was once the seat of one of the largest plantations in central N.C. Over 200 enslaved people lived and labored on the property in the decades between the American Revolution and Civil War; the historic house and surrounding landscape, now preserved as a City of Raleigh park, help illuminate the stories of their lives. Admission and hours vary.

properties.name: Mordecai Neighborhood
properties.description: The Mordecai Community of Raleigh is on the northeast corner of town, just outside the downtown area. Nearby neighborhoods include Oakwood, the city's oldest surviving neighborhood, and Brooklyn, off Glenwood Avenue.

properties.name: Morrisville History Center
properties.description: The History Center tells the story of Morrisville and the Civil War skirmish that occurred here in 1865. Includes exhibits, a touch screen with short video vignettes and a video viewing room. Hours: Mon.-Fri., 8am-5pm, except between Memorial Day and Labor Day when Town Hall closes at noon on Fri.

properties.name: Mount Hope Cemetery
properties.description: In the 1872, the City purchased 11.5 acres of property to provide additional public burial space for Raleigh's black residents. Additional burial land adjacent to the original parcel was acquired in 1895, 1912, 1914, 1926, 1945, 1947, and 1956. In 1977, the City opened Mt. Hope Cemetery to all races for burial. In 1989, the Raleigh City Council reversed its plan (dating back to 1963) to abandon the cemetery once filled and dropped interment prices. Records of interments, dating back to mid 1937, are maintained by the current Cemetery Supervisor, Danny Morgan. Among the more than 7,000 buried are Rt. Rev. Henry Beard Delany (1858-1928), Bessie Delany (1891-1995), Sadie Delany (1889-1999), William Henry Fuller (1877-1961), James H. Harris (1832-1891), Calvin E. Lightner (1877-1960) and Dr. Albert W. Pegues (1859-1923).

properties.name: Needham B. Broughton High School
properties.description: The 1929 Broughton High School was an all-white school during segregation, but its auditorium hosted the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. for a speech on Feb. 10, 1958. Dr. King spoke to an unsegregated crowd of 1,300 people, and hundreds more were turned away. (At that time, King was in the news for his successful boycott of segregated city buses in Montgomery, Ala.) “The philosophy of segregation is directly opposed to the philosophy of Christianity and to the philosophy of democracy,” Dr. King said here. In 1961 Murphey School was the testing ground for Raleigh’s school integration.

properties.name: New Bern Ave. & Edenton St. History Marker Tour
properties.description: Located within a cultural district, these long established street corridors have a rich past, tied closely to Raleigh's early history. The 1.5-mile-long History Marker Tour identifies various historic locations and occurrences along the corridors through a series of granite informational markers and historic highway signs.

properties.name: North Carolina Colored State Fair Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: Operated 1879-1930 by the North Carolina Industrial Association, cofounded by Raleigh-born brothers Charles N. Hunter (1852-1931) and Osborne Hunter. NCIA’s founders called upon Black professionals from every walk of life to attend the fair and place on exhibit “their best productions.” Over 51 years, the fair welcomed national notables including Frederick Douglass and Booker T. Washington. The fairgrounds (Brooks Ave. to Horne St. extending 55 acres north) was also site of the N.C. State Fair, 1873-1925.

properties.name: North Carolina Executive Mansion
properties.description: This fine, Victorian-style mansion, built from native materials and home to N.C. governors since 1891, was described by F.D.R. as having “the most beautiful governor’s residence interior in America.” Free admission. Tour reservations must be made at least two weeks in advance; tour hours are limited and vary seasonally.

properties.name: North Carolina Forestry Association
properties.description: The North Carolina Forestry Association (NCFA), the state’s oldest forest conservation organization, was established in 1911. Today it is a private, non-profit partnership of over 4,200 forest managers, landowners, mill operators, loggers, furniture manufacturers, educators and others concerned about the long-term health and productivity of the state’s forest resources and the industries they support.

properties.name: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
properties.description: Imagine dancing with dinosaurs, chatting amid live butterflies and meeting amongst whales. The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences is the largest natural science museum in the Southeast with four floors of exhibits, live animals, 3D movies, gift stores and two cafes. The museum also includes a Nature Research Center which is a mixture of a visitor destination, research hub and hands-on student laboratory. This one-of-a-kind unique meeting venue, capable of hosting events for up to 2,300 attendees, offers spaces ranging from board rooms to multiple floors and exhibit areas making up almost an entire wing of the museum.

properties.name: North Carolina State Archives
properties.description: The State Archives “preserves and provides access to” original and microfilm records of the colony and state of N.C. from 1663 to the present. This includes state agency/county records, private manuscript collections, maps, photographs and other documentary evidence available for research. Free admission.

properties.name: North Carolina State Capitol
properties.description: Completed in 1840, this National Historic Landmark is one of the best-preserved examples of a civic building in Greek Revival-style architecture. It originally housed the governor's office, cabinet offices, legislative chambers, state library and state geologist's office.

properties.name: North Carolina State Legislative Building
properties.description: Home of the North Carolina General Assembly, the building is unique because it is devoted solely to the legislative branch of state government. Throughout the building, provisions are made for easy public access and observation of the legislative process. Free admission. Hours: Mon.-Fri., 8am-5pm. Guided tours for 10+ available Mon.-Fri. with advance scheduling through Capital Area Visitor Services (919.733.7929).

properties.name: O'Rorke-Catholic Cemetery
properties.description: In 1858 John O'Rorke, a carriage shop owner, sold a one-and-1/8-acre parcel of land to the Catholic Church for use as a cemetery. City of Raleigh records indicate 232 transient and pauper graves are located in this cemetery, now city-owned; the last known burial was March 1986. The cemetery achieved local historic recognition when it was designated a Raleigh Historic Landmark in 2010.

properties.name: Oberlin Village
properties.description: An antebellum, free Black enclave with origins in the 1858 purchase of a 16-acre tract of land by farmer Jesse Pettiford (1792-1870); Ohio’s Oberlin College was its apparent namesake. Residents first built pioneer homes here, then vernacular and more fashionable houses by the turn of the century, dozens of which remain. Oberlin had a cemetery and its own public graded school, which predated Raleigh’s graded schools by seven years, as well as Wilson Temple United Methodist Church (ca. 1870) and Oberlin Baptist Church (ca. 1880). The village was also home to Latta University until 1920.

properties.name: Old Breastworks
properties.description: In 1863 the citizens of Raleigh gathered at the Wake County courthouse to petition the city and the state to fortify the capital city against an invasion by the Union army. On July 6, Governor Zebulon B. Vance and former Governor Thomas Bragg endorsed the decision to create a fortification of breastworks around the city.

properties.name: Olivia Raney Local History Library
properties.description: The original Olivia Raney Library opened in 1901 across from the old Capitol, moved to Fayetteville Street Mall in 1965 and closed in 1985. Today, the library’s research collection focuses on historical and genealogical materials related to Wake County and N.C., with an extensive Civil War collection and databases that provide additional resources. Free admission. Hours: Mon.-Fri.,10am-6pm; Sat., 10am-2pm.

properties.name: Page-Walker Arts and History Center
properties.description:
The historic Page-Walker Arts & History Center is a beautiful location for weddings, receptions, business meetings and social gatherings.  Hardwood floors, high ceilings, large windows and fine art provide an elegant, intimate and charming setting.  The Page-Walker's beautifully landscaped garden area is a popular site for wedding ceremonies.  The Page-Walker was built in 1868 as a railroad hotel by Town of Cary Founder, Allison Francis Page and is listed on the National Register for Historic Places.  A complete restoration in the 1990's converted the building into an arts and history for the citizens of Cary.

Today the center is alive with classes, events performances, meetings and fine arts exhibitions featuring local and regional artists' works.

properties.name: Panther Branch School (Former Juniper Level School)
properties.description: Of 20+ Rosenwald schools built in Wake County prior to 1932, only five, including this school, are visible today. Called a national treasure, these now-aging school buildings once served Black children throughout the segregated, rural South. Juniper Level School, receiving a grant from Rosenwald circa 1925-1926, was of the three-teacher type: it is a Wake County historic landmark, on the National Register of Historic Places and presently owned by Juniper Level Missionary Baptist Church.

properties.name: Pettigrew Hospital
properties.description: Site of Confederate hospital; later used by Union as U.S. Army barracks. Named for General J. Pettigrew, killed at Gettysburg in July 1863.

properties.name: Pope House Museum
properties.description:
The 1901 Pope House represents life for a prominent Black family. The house was built by Dr. Manassa Thomas Pope (1858-1934), one of the first graduates of the Leonard School of Medicine at Shaw University, an officer in an all-Black volunteer unit during the Spanish-American War and a candidate for City Council in 1919. Occupied by family members until 2000, the house contains a remarkable collection of original furnishings, artifacts and documents that date back to 1851. 

Free admission. Guided tours are offered throughout open hours.

properties.name: Preservation Zebulon
properties.description:
Preservation Zebulon Inc., is a tax-exempt non profit founded to promote the historic preservation of structures and memories in Zebulon and its surrounding areas. The area surrounding downtown is full of houses and businesses built from the time of Zebulon’s founding in 1907, and we’d like to see them preserved for future generations. Our group funded the successful nomination and led the effort to establish a Zebulon National Register Historic District, granted in August 2022.

We offer Historic Homes Tours bi-annually in the Spring, downtown historic walking tours, educational events and an annual Zebulation event to highlight our Zebulon Memory Project in the Fall. Our Zebulon Memory Project collects oral histories of the area from residents with pre- 1970 memories to share. We are also busy digitizing old photos from residents and would love to add your pre-1980 Zebulon photos to our archive.

properties.name: Prezell R. Robinson Library
properties.description: The library houses the Saint Augustine’s University Archives Room, which keeps dormant administrative records, college publications, photographs and more. The facility was made possible in 1974 and was named in honor of the eighth president of the college, Dr. Prezell R. Robinson (1967-1995), for his outstanding services. Also housed within the library are African American historical collections and the Delany sisters’ (alumnae authors of “Having Our Say”) papers and artifacts.

properties.name: Prince Hall Masonic Temple Building
properties.description: Built in 1906, the Masonic Temple served as a meeting place for Prince Hall Masons as well as an office building for Black professionals for more than a half-century. The Italianate building’s windows are accented with arched brick hoodmolds; its first story is defined by a cast-iron bracketed cornice, with its main entrance under a cutaway corner supported by a cast-iron column. The building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is now occupied by small businesses.

properties.name: Raleigh National Cemetery
properties.description: The cemetery, located in a relatively isolated area, contains a large Georgian Revival lodge and is defined by a masonry enclosure wall. Raleigh National Cemetery was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1997. The New Bern National Cemetery administers this cemetery.

properties.name: Raleigh and Gaston Railroad
properties.description: Opened in 1840 between the towns of Raleigh and Gaston, the Raleigh Gaston Railroad Line was North Carolina's second railroad. It was used heavily by Confederate troops during the Civil War. In 1967, the line merged with Seaboard Coast Line Railroad and eventually became apart of CSX.

properties.name: Rev. Plummer T. Hall House and Graves-Fields House
properties.description: Now headquarters of Preservation North Carolina, these houses (connected by a basement after being resited) are two of five Oberlin Village structures individually listed on the National Register. Both are exuberant, Queen Anne-style houses built to impress. Rev. Hall was the first pastor of Oberlin Baptist Church; Willis Graves was a bricklayer, officer of Wilson Temple United Methodist Church and justice of the peace. Both builders had been born into slavery. Spurgeon Fields, longtime employee of newspaperman Josephus Daniels, later purchased the Graves House.

properties.name: Richard B. Harrison Community Library
properties.description: Originally located on E. Hargett St. in the Delany Building, the library opened in 1935 with a collection of 890 books. Under the leadership of Mollie Huston Lee, the library’s founder and first Black public librarian in Wake County, and with strong community support, the library grew, causing it to move again before settling into its current location. The Lee Collection of more than 8,000 volumes is a major draw for researchers interested in Black history.

properties.name: Riley Hill School
properties.description: Of 20+ Rosenwald schools built in Wake County prior to 1932, only five, including this school, are visible today. Called a national treasure, these now-aging school buildings once served Black children throughout the segregated, rural South. Riley Hill School, receiving a grant from Rosenwald circa 1927-1928, was of the six-teacher type: it hosted Rosenwald himself while on a visit to Raleigh. It is on the National Register of Historic Places and presently owned by Riley Hill Baptist Church.

properties.name: Rogers-Bagley-Daniels-Pegues House
properties.description: One of the few surviving pre-Civil War houses in Raleigh, the two-story, Greek Revival-style home was built around 1855 and occupied by three prominent white families before being purchased in 1919 by its first Black owner, Dr. Albert W. Pegues, then dean of theology at Shaw University. Dr. Pegues left the house to his daughter Ernestine Hamlin (of Hamlin Drug Store). It is now owned by Shaw.

properties.name: Saint Agnes Hospital
properties.description: Sarah Hunter, wife of Saint Augustine's University’s fourth principal, founded Saint Agnes Hospital in 1896 on the college campus to provide quality medical care for Blacks. During the same time, a training school for nurses was established with the hospital. In 1937, the Training School for Nurses was accredited by the American Medical Association. The three-story, 90-bed facility served as the only hospital and training school for Blacks between Atlanta, Ga., and Washington, D.C., for nearly half a century. In 1961, Saint Agnes closed, and its patients were transferred to Wake Memorial Hospital, now known as WakeMed Health & Hospitals. Facility currently closed; renovation plans are underway.

properties.name: Saint Augustine's University
properties.description: Located on a 122-acre campus, the institution was incorporated in 1867 by the Episcopal Diocese of North Carolina to educate freed slaves. In 1928 the school became a four-year institution. Saint Augustine's University now offers more than 20 degree programs. Renowned graduates include Sadie and Bessie Delany, co-authors of “Having Our Say: The Delany Sisters’ First 100 Years.”

properties.name: Saint Augustine's University Historic Chapel
properties.description: One of the oldest buildings now on the Saint Augustine's University campus, this Norman Gothic-style chapel was built in 1895. Students constructed the irregular T-shaped chapel of native granite under the direction of Rt. Rev. Henry Beard Delany (1858-1928), who later became the first elected Black bishop in the Episcopal Church in N.C. It houses the bishop’s chair, an antique piece purchased in France as a memorial of Rt. Rev. Delany’s consecration.

properties.name: Saint Mary's School
properties.description: Saint Mary's School in Raleigh, N.C., is an independent, Episcopal, college-preparatory, girls boarding and day school dedicated to academic excellence and personal achievement for girls in grades 9-12. Five of the school's 25 buildings are Raleigh Historic Properties; the Saint Mary's Chapel, a striking neo-gothic structure that dates to 1856, and the school's front campus are listed on the National Register of Historic Places; and the campus is marked on the N.C. Civil War Trails. In 2017, Saint Mary's celebrates its 175th year of excellence in educating women. Free admission.

properties.name: Saint Matthew's School
properties.description: Of 20+ Rosenwald schools built in Wake County prior to 1932, only five, including this school, are visible today. Called a national treasure, these now-aging school buildings once served Black children throughout the segregated, rural South. St. Matthew's School, receiving a grant from Rosenwald circa 1921-1922, was of the two-teacher type: it is on the National Register of Historic Places and presently owned by St. Matthew Baptist Church. View from street; not open to the public.

properties.name: Saint Paul African Methodist Episcopal Church
properties.description: A premier example of Gothic Revival style, the present church was completed in 1910 on the site of two previous buildings. Its walls have been noted for some of the best brickwork crafted by Blacks in Raleigh, and its sanctuary has been called one of Raleigh’s most beautiful. The church has the oldest Black congregation in Wake County—originally formed by enslaved persons who had worshiped at Edenton St. United Methodist Church. In 1865 the church hosted an historic Freedmen’s Convention.

properties.name: Second Empire Restaurant & Tavern
properties.description:
Located in the elegantly restored Dodd-Hinsdale house (1879), Second Empire combines history, atmosphere and gourmet cuisine for an unforgettable dining experience.  
AAA Four Diamond Award and Wine Spectator Award of Excellence, DiRona Award.

properties.name: South Park and East Raleigh
properties.description: A 30-block area that is Raleigh’s largest, historically Black neighborhood. It developed mainly from 1865 to 1940. The core neighborhood of South Park, a 1907 subdivision, was partly developed by Black educator and businessman Dr. Edward Johnson. Shaw University was also key to the growth of the area, which still features historic shotgun houses and triple-A cottages as well as side-gabled, front-gabled and hipped-roof homes.

properties.name: Spring Hill House
properties.description:
The Spring Hill House, part of North Carolina State University's Centennial Campus, currently houses the N.C. Japan Center. The house is a registered historic building, built about 1815 in the Georgian style as the main house of a plantation. It stands on a rise southwest of downtown Raleigh, and the name refers to a spring of water arising at the foot of the hill. 


The Spring Hill House has undergone changes during its two centuries of existence. For example, it lost the second story of its original two-storied, Doric-columned porch, and the south wall lost two external chimneys and a direct entrance to the large parlor. It has also benefited from major repairs, including a major structural overhaul in 2000-2001. The house is open for your examination during N.C. Japan Center office hours. A more detailed account of its history and features, prepared while the building was in use by Dorothea Dix Hospital (and from which most of this account was compiled), is available in English upon request.


It is an honor for the N.C. Japan Center to be able to carry on its services in this beautiful building, so closely linked to the history of N.C.

properties.name: Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee Highway Historical Marker
properties.description: Two months after Woolworth sit-ins in nearby Durham and Greensboro, about 150 student leaders from 10 states met at Shaw University for the Southwide Leadership Conference on Nonviolent Resistance to Segregation, Apr. 15-17, 1960. The session, convened by the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, ultimately created the “Temporary Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee” (later SNCC). The organization’s members became frontline leaders in the civil rights movement. The Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., visiting on Apr. 16, also spoke to 1,600 assembled at nearby Memorial Auditorium.

properties.name: Sugar Magnolia Cafe & Emporium
properties.description: Sugar Magnolia is a cafe, tea house, restaurant and art emporium in historic Wake Forest. Experience great coffee, tea and  food, as well as shopping for locally produced art, jewelry, crafts and more.

properties.name: Terry Sanford Federal Building & U.S. Courthouse
The Carolinian Newspaper
properties.description: A Black newspaper founded in 1940 by P.R. Jervay Sr., the paper published seven editions, which were circulated in major cities throughout N.C. Today “The Carolinian” is the only Black newspaper published twice weekly in the state. The newspaper remains family-owned and operated and is currently run by co-publishers Paul R. and Evelyn H. Jervay.

properties.name: Town of Morrisville
properties.description: The Morrisville History Center in the lobby of Town Hall tells the story of Morrisville and the Civil War skirmish that occurred here in 1865. The History Center includes exhibits, a touch screen with short video vignettes several longer videos.

properties.name: Tupper Memorial Baptist Church
properties.description: Founded by Dr. Henry Martin Tupper in 1866 as the Second Baptist Church and reportedly boasting the largest Sunday School in North Carolina then, with some 1,000 students. Between 1912 and 1913, the congregation renamed itself the Blount St. Baptist Church and constructed a new wood-frame building on the site of the original church. In the 1940s, the church was renamed again to honor Dr. Tupper, and it was veneered with brick in 1957. Dr. Tupper also founded nearby Shaw University.

properties.name: W. N. H. Smith
properties.description: With his election to the Confederate Congress in 1861, he sought to avert secession. Once war was declared, Smith served in the Congress for the remainder of the conflict.

properties.name: W.E.B. DuBois School
properties.description: Of 20+ Rosenwald schools built in Wake County prior to 1932, only five, including this school, are visible today. Called a national treasure, these now-aging school buildings once served Black children throughout the segregated, rural South. The DuBois School, receiving a grant from Rosenwald circa 1925-1926, was of the seven-teacher type: it operated as Wake Forest Middle School from the 1960s-1989 and was on the National Register of Historic Places. Now ruinous; view from street.

properties.name: Wake Forest University
properties.description: Opened 1834 as Wake Forest College; closed 1862 due to faculty and students enlisting in the Confederate Army.

properties.name: Wendell Historic Trail
properties.description: The Wendell Historical Society's Wendell Historic Trail offers a map of more than 15 historic homes, places and National Register Historic Districts in and around the town of Wendell.

properties.name: Wendell Museum
properties.description: The Wendell Museum is home to the Wendell Historical Society. The community of Wendell is rich in history and culture. The museum celebrates Wendell and is run by a group of volunteers who are passionate about preserving the town's history. The museum has an extensive library of documents and photos that tell the story of Wendell's past.

properties.name: William Peace University, Main Building
properties.description: An impressive Greek Revival structure used during the Civil War as a hospital; from 1865 to 1869, it served as the headquarters for the central administrative district of the Freedmen’s Bureau. Later during Reconstruction, the building was reclaimed for use as a girls’ school and is now a four-year, coeducational college. Hours: by appointment only.

properties.name: William W. Holden
properties.description: The only Chief Executive in North Carolina history to be impeached and removed from office (and the first in the nation to endure that indignity), William Woods Holden (1818-1892) was a central figure in the North Carolina's Civil War and Reconstruction era. His home stood at the location of the historical marker. Holden’s house, at the corner of Hargett and McDowell Streets in Raleigh, was razed in 1925 to make way for the Professional Building now on the site.

properties.name: Zebulon Town Hall
properties.description: Zebulon's Town Hall is located in the historic Wakelon School, which had been renovated by GlaxoSmithKline as a training facility prior to its repurposing by the town. The distinctive structure opened in 1909 as one of four, county high schools, and today this historic building is a reminder of N.C.'s dramatic early 20th-century progress in public education.

properties.name: Ann and Jim Goodnight Museum Park at North Carolina Museum of Art
properties.description: The 164-acre Ann and Jim Goodnight Museum Park and its trail system welcome visitors through natural areas and to more than a dozen commissioned works of art. Designed for walking, cycling and jogging, the paved trails connect to the Capital Area Greenway System. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: Falls Lake State Recreation Area
properties.description: One of the largest recreational facilities in the state, offering a wide variety of activities. Camping, hiking, fishing, boating and swimming are available, as well as picnic areas and playgrounds. Hours: Daily, 8am-sunset approximately; call or visit website. To make camping reservations go to www.ncparks.gov or call 1.877.7CAMPNC.

properties.name: Fantasy Lake Adventure Park
properties.description:
As the largest scuba diving park on the East Coast, Fantasy Lake Adventure Park offers a wide range of scuba-diving recreational activities. Beginning with a 100-acre, scenic natural environment that is carefully landscaped and maintained, Fantasy Lake promotes an enjoyable and refreshing experience.

Fantasy Lake Adventure Park also offers 14 small campsites, three large group campsites and two large campgrounds located within easy access to lake diving. All campsites are for primitive camping only.

properties.name: North Carolina State Fairgrounds
properties.description: Eight facilities plus two facilities/grounds which house the state’s largest indoor/outdoor flea market. The grounds also offer 350 full-service RV access sites, and amenities include free parking in addition to convenient access from I-40, I-440 and I-540. Events are staged at the fairgrounds year-round; call or visit website. Private catering service is available.

properties.name: Falls Lake State Recreation Area
properties.description: One of the largest recreational facilities in the state, offering a wide variety of activities. Camping, hiking, fishing, boating and swimming are available, as well as picnic areas and playgrounds. Hours: Daily, 8am-sunset approximately; call or visit website. To make camping reservations go to www.ncparks.gov or call 1.877.7CAMPNC.

properties.name: Lakeside Retreats
properties.description: Lakeside Retreats welcomes you to our little escape from day to day life. Located just 20 minutes from downtown Raleigh, Lakeside is a family friendly campground with fun for all.

properties.name: Tamasha Modern Indian Kitchen
properties.description: An ode to modern Indian cuisine. Chef Bhavin Chhatwani, with a Michelin-star experience, serves progressive creations, craft cocktails and an extensive wine list in a stellar ambiance.

properties.name: Brodeto
properties.description:
At Brodeto, renowned Chef Scott Crawford pays homage to the Adriatic Sea, spotlighting the culinary traditions of Southern Italy and Croatia. Our menu emphasizes lighter, seafood-centric dishes, reflecting the diverse and vibrant tastes of these coastal regions.

Complimenting these offerings, Beverage Manager Jordan Joseph has curated a menu of coastal-inspired cocktails, amari, and herbal liqueurs, alongside a diverse array of wines from Italy, Croatia, and the broader Adriatic area.

properties.name: La Terrazza Raleigh
properties.description: La Terrazza presents a delightful fusion of southern Italian and Mediterranean cuisine, complemented by an enchanting city skyline view. With seasonal delicacies, premium ingredients, and market-fresh produce, our menu showcases traditional favorites with innovative flair. Step into our inviting dining space adorned with floor-to-ceiling glass walls, or unwind at one of our two bars – one indoors and the other nestled in a patio enclosure. We aim to whisk you away to a culinary experience like no other.

properties.name: (Ish) Delicatessen
properties.description: (ish) delicatessen is a deli and sandwich shop in downtown Raleigh offering counter service.

properties.name: 1 in 6 Snacks
properties.description:
1 in 6 Snacks represents the one in six people in 2016 that did not know where their next meal will come from. The first snack food offered is Carolina Kettle potato chips, and with each bag sold they donate a portion of the proceeds to the local food bank. By purchasing these chips, you will be donating five cents to a local Food Bank.


The freshly cooked chips are seasoned to perfection with a unique source of real Carolina spices, herbs and flavors. All of the quality snacks are made to satisfy with bold tastes that reflect the traditional Southern recipes that will make your mouth water.

properties.name: 10th & Terrace at Residence Inn Raleigh Downtown
properties.description: Located on the 10th floor rooftop terrace & bar at the Residence Inn Raleigh Downtown, 10th and Terrace allows you to indulge in a perfectly poured cocktail, fine wine, or local craft beer. Their kitchen features flavorful Contemporary American Fusion small plates with North Carolina accents.

properties.name: 1250 Heritage
properties.description: Open to members and the public, 1250 Heritage is located in the Heritage Golf Clubhouse in the heart of the Heritage Wake Forest community. With its casual, elegant dining atmosphere, stunning views, tempting menus and comfortable sophistication, 1250 is the perfect place to entertain clients, enjoy leisurely lunches and join friends for dinner. Warm woods, flat-screen televisions and all ABC permits in the bar offer a perfect place for post-golf-round relaxing or an evening out.

properties.name: 13 Tacos & Taps
properties.description: 13 Tacos & Taps offers a Mexican fusion menu with craft beer from your favorite local breweries plus specialty drinks from the bar! A whole new concept!

properties.name: 41Hundred at Renaissance Raleigh North Hills Hotel
properties.description:
41Hundred and 41Hundred Lounge are seated in the elegant Renaissance Raleigh North Hills hotel. With a focus on fresh, local, high quality ingredients and simple yet memorable food and drink, 41Hundred is a must when looking for North Hills restaurants.
The ambience is casual, and weekly evening entertainment enhances the experience whether you're stopping in for house-aged whiskey, a shareable plate or locally made ice cream sold exclusively here. Serving breakfast both buffet style and a la carte, lunch and dinner in the lounge, along with the full bar experience.
Photo: Stacey Sprenz Photography

properties.name: 42nd St. Oyster Bar & Seafood Grill
properties.description: The 42nd St. Oyster Bar is one of the truly famous eating establishments in N.C. In spite of all the stories and myths about the place, people could always come and have great steamed oysters and cold beer. The famous old place has developed the reputation of being one of the most enjoyable restaurants to frequent in the southern part of the United States.

properties.name: A Place At The Table
properties.description:
Raleigh needs a place where all people can EAT. Raleigh needs a place where COMMUNITY can be built. Why does Raleigh need such a café? We have soup kitchens, we have nice restaurants, but we do not have a place that brings us all together to eat.

Mission: A Place at the Table provides community and healthy food for all regardless of means.

Vision: A Place at the Table is a welcoming and inviting space that provides an opportunity for all people to come and experience conversation and community while enjoying an excellent, fresh and healthy meal. People long for a community, a place to fit in, a place to feel welcome and a place to be a part of something bigger than just themselves.

We are a pay-what-you-can cafe.

What does this mean if you want to eat here?

You have five options:


	Pay what you are able to afford.
	Pay what you would typically pay for a similar meal. (We will have a suggested donation)
	Pay what you would typically pay, plus an extra donation.
	Pay specifically for someone else’s full meal.
	Pay by volunteering with us.


We believe in A Place at the Table. We believe in our core values and believe that this will work. We want to invite all people to engage in community with us and engage in community with others.

properties.name: A Taste of Brooklyn
properties.description:
Located in the historic downtown district of Apex, Buttercream’s Bakeshop is the destination for delicious and beautiful cakes, cupcakes and cookies.

Our famous European Buttercream teamed with our decadent Southern Buttercream makes our cakes simply the best for every taste.

Tina Yuhl, owner, pastry chef and professionally trained graduate of the Institute of Culinary Education, trained at many of the "who's who of" NYC Restaurants.

properties.name: A'Nets Katch
properties.description: The A'Nets Katch is committed to serving only the finest foods, made with the freshest ingredients. All of our dishes are made to order, no heat lamps here. Our little spot and friendly staff will create your plate for you to dine in or takeout. A'Nets Katch also sells fresh seafood and caters with our mobile kitchen.

properties.name: A'Verde Cocina and Tequila Library
properties.description: A’Verde is a Mexican restaurant inspired by “Top Chef” alum Katsuji Tanabe’s desire to bring fresh, vibrant, delicious, and fun flavors to the table. Drawing on his Mexican heritage, the menu is full of memories and stories of family recipes and experiences. Don’t expect traditional Mexican fare, while dishes will be familiar and comforting, these flavors will be on trend with N.C.’s best seasonal ingredients or the latest hot culinary or beverage movement. A’Verde’s desire is to give friends a relaxed, creative, and exciting experience.

properties.name: Abbey Road Tavern & Grill - Apex
properties.description: Burgers, Beer, Music... Abbey Road Tavern & Grill thrives to provide you with excellent service. These things all seem to "Come Together" at Abbey Road!

properties.description: Burgers, Beer, Music... Abbey Road Tavern & Grill thrives to provide you with excellent service. These things all seem to "Come Together" at Abbey Road!

properties.name: Academy Street Bistro
properties.description: Academy Street Bistro is a casual dining restaurant serving a new American cuisine menu with a French flare. Come try the fresh fish, all natural meats, fresh and local produce. Academy Street Bistro only uses the freshest and highest quality ingredients available. They are committed to local farmers and use organic produce whenever possible. The meats are all natural with no added antibiotics or hormones. Academy Street Bistro is also very conscientious towards food allergies and especially welcome gluten-free Individuals.

properties.name: Acme Pizza Co.
properties.description:
Acme Pizza Co. serves Chicago style deep dish pizza, hand-tossed thin pizza, select pastas, salads and has 18 beers on tap.
Photo via the restaurant

properties.name: Acme Pizza Co. - Morrisville
properties.description: Acme Pizza Co. serves Chicago style deep dish pizza, hand-tossed thin pizza, select pastas, salads and has 18 beers on tap.

properties.name: Agave Mexican Bar & Grill
properties.description: Agave Mexican Bar & Grill serves Mexican and American fare including fajitas, tacos, ceviche and tilapia.

properties.name: Aggie's Grill Station
properties.description: Aggie's Grill Station is a hidden gem on Capital Blvd. offering a variety of cuisines.

properties.name: Ajisai Japanese Fusion
properties.description: Located in Cameron Village. Ajisai breaks new ground with innovated modern decor, intimate full bar and by serving extensive selections of fine, fresh fish. Ajisai turns the art of eating, whether by yourself or with a group of friends, into an experience which will never be forgotten.

properties.name: Ajja
properties.description:
The Hindi/Urdu word for “come over,” Ajja invokes a destination that is celebratory and inviting. Led by James Beard Foundation Award-nominated chef/owner Cheetie Kumar, returning Garland team members Gaëlle Laforest, general manager and Lindsay Ogden, beverage manager, round out the service team. Chef de Cuisine Scott McKenney, and chefs Sarah Kenney and Chris Gamble join Chef Kumar in the kitchen to develop the menu.

Ajja’s menu draws inspiration from the diverse foodways and cultures, vibrant spices, and cooking techniques of the Mediterranean, the Middle East and beyond. Building on Garland’s legacy, Ajja continues telling the rich story of North Carolina’s growers, farmers and purveyors in a vibrant indoor-outdoor neighborhood restaurant.

properties.name: Akami Sushi Bar
properties.description: Akami Sushi Bar is locally owned and operated offering only sushi (+ Japanese sake, beer & wine). We offer great quality fish, but in a very affordable price that everyone can enjoy. We also offer Omakase on Friday and Saturday nights. Call to reserve.

properties.name: Akari Express
properties.description: Akari Express offers authentic and delicious tasting Japanese and Asian cuisine.  Akari Express's convenient location and affordable prices make our restaurant a natural choice for dine-in or take-out.

properties.name: Aladdin's Eatery - Brier Creek
properties.description: Dedicated to excellent customer service and providing the highest quality, unique, natural foods of the Middle East, while at the same time catering to customers' increased awareness and concern regarding health and nutrition.

properties.name: Aladdin's Eatery - North Hills
properties.description: Aladdin’s Eatery, serves guests healthy and flavorful Lebanese-American foods that align with their dietary preferences and requirements.

properties.name: Alexander's Mediterranean Cuisine
properties.description: Alexander’s honors the breadth of traditional Greek cuisine by bringing fresh, wholesome dishes from all regions of Greece to an elegant, contemporary and comfortable setting near the Raleigh area. Entrees cover a range of seafood, chicken and beef in addition to traditional Greek specialties such as Moussaka, Souvlaki and Shrimp Alexander. Alexander's signature dishes are Lamb Shank (baked with potatoes, carrots and celery in tomato wine sauce) and Rack of Lamb (grilled and served with roasted potatoes, vegetables and mint jelly sauce).

properties.name: Alimentari at Left Bank - Transfer Co. Food Hall
properties.description: Alimentari at Left Bank is a collaboration between Josh DeCarolis of Durham's Mother & Sons and Left Bank Butchery out of Saxapahaw, N.C. featuring fresh pasta by the pound, Italian tigelles and a whole a butchery/charcuterie shop.

properties.name: Alpaca Peruvian Charcoal Chicken - Apex
properties.description: Alpaca is recognized for its unforgettable rotisserie chicken, cooked in a special marinade, then roasted in their imported oven from Peru. This oven uses only wood charcoal, no gas or electric heat is needed. This charcoal roasting method is the source of the mouth watering smell as you approach the restaurant! Alpaca pairs their chicken with traditional South American sides — from Plantains to Yuca Fries or black beans.

properties.name: Amber Flavors and Taste
properties.description: Amber Cary is a modern Indian restaurant that is home to the largest community in North Carolina. With our contemporary recipes exquisitely curated by our expert chefs, you will find everything for your palette whichever nationality you belong to.

properties.name: Amedeo's Italian Restaurant
properties.description: Decked out in Wolfpack memorabilia, Amedeo's has served Raleigh family-recipe Italian cuisine since 1963.

properties.name: Amitie Macaron - Morgan Street Food Hall
properties.description: Amitie Macarons is a home-based start-up bakery located in Raleigh, N.C., specializing only in creating “French Macaron” cookies. Find them for sale within Morgan Street Food Hall!

properties.name: Amorino
properties.description: Amorino delights connoisseurs around the world with its finest quality gelato, which is made according to traditional Italian methods. The taste of each gelato is not only dependent on the most rigorous selection of sourced ingredients but also on the patience and the attentiveness of highly trained chefs during its preparation. Amorino insists on using only organic and natural products, paying particular attention origins of each ingredient and also by monitoring production methods. Enjoy Italian gelato at its finest. Macarons, chocolates, sweets, hot drinks and milkshakes also available.

properties.name: Andia's Ice Cream - Southeast Cary
properties.description: Andia's is a local, family business that is woman-owned and operated. We are proud to be a national award winning ice cream made with premium ingredients. Our shop offers a large variety of decadent flavors as well as a vegan flavor and two sorbets, always available for our lactose-intolerant and vegan friends!

properties.name: Andia's Ice Cream - West Cary
properties.description: Andia's is a local, family business that is woman-owned and operated. We are proud to be a national award winning ice cream made with premium ingredients. Our shop offers a large variety of decadent flavors as well as a vegan flavor and two sorbets, always available for our lactose-intolerant and vegan friends!

properties.name: Angie's Restaurant
properties.description: Serving traditional Southern breakfast and lunch, from 5:30am to 2:30pm, Mon. thru Sat. Come on by, bring the family and enjoy some great Southern cooking!

properties.name: Anise Pho
properties.description: Anise Pho serves authentic Vietnamese cuisine as well as bubble tea, smoothie and vegetarian options.

properties.name: Anna's Gourmet Goodies
properties.description:
Anna’s Gourmet Goodies makes, bakes and ships gourmet cookie and brownie gifts to recipients throughout the United States and to Military bases around the globe.  Perfect for clients, prospects, employees, friends and family. Made from scratch. Baked fresh. Shipped direct.

For business clients, we offer a custom note card and label with your logo and branding.  No setup fee and no minimum order.  We offer managed gift services for birthdays, anniversaries and follow up gifts.  Send us the list and we manage delivery.

properties.name: Anna's Pizzeria - Apex
properties.description:
Anna’s Pizzeria is a busy, family-friendly restaurant serving up authentic New York style pizzas and Italian dishes located in historic downtown Apex.
Photo via the restaurant

properties.name: Anna's Pizzeria - Fuquay-Varina
properties.description: Anna’s Pizzeria is a busy, family-friendly restaurant serving up authentic New York style pizzas and Italian dishes located in historic downtown Fuquay-Varina.

properties.name: Annelore's German Bakery
properties.description: Annelore's German Bakery creates authentic German pastries from scratch and brings them to a market near you! Pastries are made using the finest local ingredients, including Bee Blessed honey, Godwin Farm apples, Britt Farm pears, and Redbud Farms certified organic ginger, tomatoes, and basil, when available. Annelore's doesn't use preservatives, dough enhancers, or additives in any of their signature pastries. Fresh and local!

properties.name: Another Broken Egg Cafe - Midtown
properties.description: When it comes to breakfast, brunch or lunch... Another Broken Egg Cafe offers a totally egg-ceptional experience! Serve exceptionally fresh and nutritional food with over 114 menu items to choose from for your breakfast, brunch and lunch experience.

properties.name: Another Broken Egg Cafe - Morrisville
properties.description: Serving fresh and nutritional food with over 130 menu items to choose from for your breakfast, brunch, and lunch experience.

properties.name: Apex Wings
properties.description: An easy going and laid back, family owned and operated, neighborhood pub and restaurant specializing in Buffalo style chicken wings.

properties.name: Arandas Mexican Cuisine
properties.description: Arandas Mexican Cuisine brings to Apex decades of experience in Mexican cuisine, with a wide range of common dishes along with unique specialties. Come give them a try!

properties.name: Arepa Culture
properties.description:
Arepa Culture's specialty is an Arepa, pronounced (ah-reh-pah), a gluten-free white cornmeal “bread” that we handcraft, grill and generously fill with a variety of our delicious, quality ingredients.

We are a family-owned and operated food truck and storefront that serves gourmet-style Venezuelan cuisine. Our food truck is inspired by the Latin American culture with many local and organic products for an authentic, mouthwatering experience. Our Arepas, in addition to all of the ingredients we use, are 100% GLUTEN-FREE. We also offer Vegetarian and Vegan options and can accommodate any dietary restrictions.

properties.name: Armando's Pizza
properties.description: Armando's Pizza offers a slice of New York! Enjoy NY-style pizza, stromboli, and other Italian staples.

properties.name: Artylicious Cakes
properties.description:
Artylicious Cakes' goal is to put a smile on your face as you experience a beautiful and truly delicious unique piece of cake art.

Artylicious Cakes specializes in custom cakes of all kinds, for any occasion. They are not your average bakery, grocery store or discount warehouse club that bakes cakes and sits them out for people to purchase. All of their work is customized to your specific request and made fresh for each order.

properties.name: Asali Desserts & Cafe
properties.description: Asali Desserts & Cafe offers desserts, small plates, and coffee at MacGregor Village in Cary,.

properties.name: Ashworth Drugs
properties.description:
Since 1957, Ashworth's has been the place to get your medications and kick back with a homemade orangeade or a coke float, and chow down on a delicious hot dog and think back to a simpler time.
Photo: Selena N. B. H.

properties.name: Assaggio's Italian Bistro
properties.description: With a dream, the love of good Italian food, and the enjoyment and appreciation derived from cooking and preparing food for the enjoyment of others, Dean Biales opened Assaggio’s Italian restaurant in April of 2004. Originally from Long Island, New York, Dean followed that dream to Raleigh, NC and the rest is history.

properties.name: Assaggio's Pizzeria & Ristorante
properties.description: Assaggio's provides fresh, delicious, New York style hand-tossed pizza, scrumptious entrees, delicious sub sandwiches, ice-cold beverages and quality wine.

properties.name: Asuka Asian Bistro (Wake Forest)
properties.description: Asuka Asian Bistro is a Japanese-styled restaurant serving great sushi and traditional Japanese foods.

properties.name: Aubrey's and Peedie's Grill
properties.description: ﻿Aubrey's and Peedie's is a local fixture in Wendell. They serve all the Southern specialties: country ham, creamy grits, fluffy homemade biscuits with sausage gravy. On Saturday morning you'll find a long table full of locals who have been meeting here for breakfast for years. They are open Monday thru Saturday, closed on Sunday.

properties.name: Aversboro Restaurant & Sports Bar
properties.description: Come and sit on our newly decorated, outdoor patio, with plants, sunscreens and fans in the summer and heaters in the winter. Come inside the sports bar and enjoy one of the 10 flat screen TV's where the game or event you want to watch will be on. If you want a quiet dinner, then come up top to the family friendly restaurant.

properties.name: Aviator SmokeHouse
properties.description:
Aviator SmokeHouse features smoked wings…that are deep fried to order, homemade onion rings, smoked pork pulled and chopped Eastern NC style! They have St. Louis style smoke ribs that can be served dry-rubbed or with any of our house made sauces. All their food is made in house. We strive to source all of our vegetables locally and all their pork comes from North Carolina. They strive to be farm to table.
Be wary of their wing sauces they can be much spicier than others. Their MocoLoco sauce is made with the Ghost Chile Pepper which contains approximately 1million Scoville units of heat! Their other sauces Crazy, Monster, Buffalo, BlackMamba and Aviator are all created in house using beer!

properties.name: Aviator Taphouse Gastropub
properties.description: All brewery beers on tap (also brewery made Rootbeer). Aviator services HotRod Red, Old BullDog ESB, Devil’s Tramping Ground Tripel, CaveMan Alt, SteamHead, King Rat Oatmeal Stout, Gremlin’s Golden and FrostNipper Winter Ale.

properties.name: Awaze Cuisine
properties.description: A small family owned business located in Cary, featuring an authentic Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine. Awaze is a condiment mix of garlic, wine and berbere, which results in dark red, spicy paste then used in some dishes or as a side condiment. Awaze serves lunch and dinner while offering a variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian meals. You have the option to make your food mild, medium or spicy. Bring your family and friends to enjoy this unique dining experience!

properties.name: Axis Restaurant and Bar (Embassy Suites by Hilton Raleigh Crabtree)
Azurelise Chocolate Truffles
properties.description: Azurelise makes chocolate gift shopping for hard to please chocolate enthusiasts fun, stress and risk free. Since 2002, the flavors on Azurelise's chocolate truffle menu have delighted the palates of chocolate lovers worldwide, chocolate lovers who won't settle for less than the gold standard. Azurelise chocolate truffles are that standard. Order online or visit the Azurelise kiosk to purchase ready to go boxes of milk and dark chocolate classic, sea salt caramel and chocolate truffle assortments.

properties.name: BJ's Restaurant and Brewhouse
properties.description: California-twist on Chicago Deep Dish Pizza, award-winning craft beers, signature Pizookie® dessert, a menu of Better for You entrees, handcrafted burgers and specialty entrees... all of this and more can be found at BJ's Restaurant and Brewhouse!

properties.name: Ba-Da Wings - Creedmoor Crossing
properties.description: Your neighborhood bar and wing joint! Come in and try out local beers. With more than a dozen taps, 40 bottled and canned beers and a full bar, Ba Da Wings has something for everyone! What goes better with cold beer than hot wings! Enjoy a full menu to satisfy the hungriest of taste buds.

properties.name: Babymoon Cafe
properties.description: Babymoon Cafe provides comfortable fine dining and catering from brown-bag to black-tie. Enjoy delicious homemade meals any time, including a variety of pizzas, pastas, seafood, steaks, salads and more. Babymoon Cafe takes great pride in the Italian culinary tradition.

properties.name: Backfins Crabhouse
properties.description:
They've re-created that tradition here with tables covered in brown paper and mallets for cracking the shells of the house specialty, steamed crabs. They're offered in any quantity you like, from a single crab to the $24.95 all you can eat Crab Feast. 


The brothers are also proud of their Maryland style crab cakes, which John Jenkins says are "all jumbo lump, with just enough cracker to hold them together." Other options include peel and eat shrimp, oysters and clams on the half shell and Southern fried seafood platters. There's a modest wine selection and beers are -- true to crab shack tradition -- available by the bottle only.

properties.name: Bad Cat Coffee, Crepes, & Bagels - Morgan Street Food Hall
properties.description: Bad Cat Coffee, Crepes, & Bagels brings you exceptional locally roasted coffee, tender made-to-order crepes (both savory & sweet) and the best darn bagels in the Research Triangle Region. Bad Cat believes in fun and adventure with signature drinks such as the Caramel Meow-chiatto & the Calico Cat Mocha—soooo good it will make ya’ meow!

properties.name: Bad Daddy's Burger Bar
properties.description: Bad Daddy’s Burger Bar is one bite away from becoming your favorite neighborhood spot. They are a chef driven burger joint that uses a mix of local and artisanal ingredients to make the most amazing burger you’ve ever had. They work hard to make sure anything they serve is the best possible product and make everything in their scratch kitchen.

properties.name: Bad Daddy's Burger Bar - Falls of Neuse
properties.description: Bad Daddy’s Burger Bar is one bite away from becoming your favorite neighborhood spot. They are a chef driven burger joint that uses a mix of local and artisanal ingredients to make the most amazing burger you’ve ever had. They work hard to make sure anything they serve is the best possible product and make everything in their scratch kitchen.

properties.name: Bad Daddy's Burger Bar - Morrisville
properties.description: Bad Daddy’s Burger Bar is one bite away from becoming your favorite neighborhood spot. They are a chef driven burger joint that uses a mix of local and artisanal ingredients to make the most amazing burger you’ve ever had. They work hard to make sure anything they serve is the best possible product and make everything in their scratch kitchen.

properties.name: Bahama Breeze
properties.description: At Bahama Breeze, you can enjoy great food, tropical cocktails and music in an island setting.

properties.name: Baja Burrito
properties.description: California-style Taqueria with fresh food cooked daily, and lots of it! Burritos, Tacos, Nachos, Quesadillas and Taco and Baja Salads available.

properties.name: Bakery La Dolce Vita
properties.description: Bakery La Dolce Vita offers an assortment of cookies, breads, muffins, pastries, croissants, danishes and various other baked goods.

properties.name: Bali Hai
properties.description: Bali Hai has been part of the Triangle for more than 20 years, bringing authentic Mongolian food to Garner.

properties.name: Baltic Bites
properties.description: After spending most of our lives in Lithuania, a country with less than 3 million people, we decided to share our culture with the rest of the world, especially Raleigh, a city that's full of diversity. Baltic Bites began its journey a little over a year and a half ago in the Triangle, with the expectation of breaking the norm and big hopes to expand. Owner/Chef Dana Senfeldiene, partners with Kent Lehman and Ginter Senfeldas - striving to share quality authentic and European cuisine that can be mistaken for American comfort food. A year and a half later, Baltic Bites remains the first and only Lithuanian food truck in the U.S - It just doesn't get more diverse than that.

properties.name: Bar Louie
properties.description: Bar Louie is an eclectic urban bar made famous for signature martinis, cocktails and dynamic beer selection. Eat. Drink. Be Happy.

properties.name: Barcelona Wine Bar
properties.description: Barcelona Wine Bar & Restaurant is a warm and welcoming tapas bar inspired by the culture of Spain. The ever-changing menu is focused on clean flavors, seasonal ingredients, specialties from Spain and the Mediterranean, and rustic small plate presentations created by chefs with tremendous talent. Barcelona offers an award-winning selection of wines from Spain and South America—and boasts as one of the largest Spanish wine programs in the U.S.

properties.name: Barry's Cafe
properties.description: Barry's Cafe is open Monday - Tuesday 7 a.m. - 2 p.m.; Wednesday - Saturday 7:00 a.m. - 8:30 p.m. and Sunday 8 a.m. - 1 p.m. for breakfast only.

properties.name: Baton Rouge Cuisine
properties.description:
The Baton Rouge Cuisine food truck serves Cajun food to the Raleigh, N.C. area and is owned by former Harlem Globetrotters Anthony “Airport” Greenup.  After a nine year professional basketball career with the world-renowned Harlem Globetrotters, Anthony decided to pursue his other dream of owning a food business. This is how mobile food business Baton Rouge Cuisine began!

Baton Rouge Cuisine is family-owned and operated food truck in the triangle area (North Carolina). Our food is cooked fresh daily and created to fill your belly.

properties.name: Bazil Indian Cuisine
properties.description:
Welcome to Bazil Indian Cuisine, a truly unique dining experience in Raleigh, NC. Our restaurant is not just a place to enjoy delicious food; it’s an enchanting story waiting to be savored. At Bazil Indian Cuisine, we pride ourselves on pushing culinary boundaries and introducing new flavors to the vibrant Indian food community in Raleigh. Led by a passionate mother, our restaurant offers an extensive wine list that perfectly complements our fusion menu. Prepare to be captivated by our assortment of dishes, including delicacies like sea bass, lobster, and octopus – offerings that you won’t find in other Indian restaurants. We believe in creating an unforgettable experience for our guests, where every bite is an adventure of flavors and textures.As a family-owned establishment, we strive to create a warm and welcoming atmosphere where families and friends can come together to celebrate life’s moments. Whether you’re a seasoned foodie or new to Indian cuisine, we invite you to embark on a culinary journey with us. Come and discover the vibrant world of Bazil Indian Cuisine, where tradition meets innovation, and taste buds are delighted.

The top-rated Indian restaurant in Raleigh is currently Bazil Indian Cuisine.

properties.name: Bean Sprouts
properties.description: Featuring good-for-you dining options, Bean Sprouts helps fuel healthy bodies as children and families build healthy minds. The café features an award-winning menu that empowers kids to make their own healthy choices. Grown-ups will be equally pleased with sophisticated sandwich, salad and pizza options along with the organic espresso bar. Bean Sprouts intentionally partners with family destinations that fit its “HIPP” core values – health, innovation, positivity and playfulness. The café’s location at Marbles means children and families can take a break from learning through play, refuel with healthy food and get right back into the museum.

properties.name: Beasley's Chicken + Honey
properties.description:
An Ashley Christensen restaurant, Beasley's Chicken + Honey does fried chicken. Fried quarter chicken, chicken biscuits and fried chicken and waffles are the staples here, along with a variety of great tasting southern sides like "big bad" bacon and Yukon potato salad. Local beers and delicious cakes and pies cap off the menu.

Photo credits: AC Restaurants

properties.name: Bee BahnMi
properties.description: A fast-casual restaurant offering the world's best street food, Vietnamese banh mi.

properties.name: Belgian Waffle Crafters
properties.description: Belgian Waffle Crafters is the first one and only Belgian waffle food truck in the Triangle. They are Belgian and they’ll bring to you what they do the best: Liege waffles! Come eat a delicious sweet or savory, made from scratch, Belgian Waffle.

properties.name: Bella Italia Ristorante (Wake Forest)
properties.description: Proudly using only the finest ingredients, you won't find anything pre-made, but hand-made fresh to order here. From N.Y. Style Pizza to Cheese Steak Subs, from rich Fettuccine Alfredo to tender Veal Marsala, you're sure to find something to satisfy your craving.

properties.name: Bella Monica
properties.description: This neighborhood trattoria, Bella Monica, has become an extension of Nana's table. A place for family and friends to relax and bond over pasta and wine.

properties.name: Bella's Wood Fired Pizza & Tapas - Morgan Street Food Hall
properties.description: Bella’s is proud to be bringing its wood-fired pizzas to Morgan Street Food Hall & Market.  Patrons can expect a high quality pizza from the freshest ingredients all day long.  Bella’s also offers a creative seasonal small plate tapas menu for the discerning consumer.

properties.name: Benchwarmers Bagels - Transfer Co. Food Hall
properties.description: Benchwarmers Bagels is a collaboration from the masterminds behind Jubala Coffee and Boulted Bread, providing wood-fired bagels daily and fresh coffee.

properties.name: Benny Capitale's
properties.description: Benny Capitale’s keeps it simple, to the point. Pizza, by the slice. We opened in 2017 on our favorite block in Raleigh, on Fayetteville exactly in between the capitol building and the infamous Raleigh Times. The buck stops here in North Carolina, and for 5 bucks you can get a full meal, just the way old school Raleigh would’ve liked it.

properties.name: Benny's Billiards & Sports Bar
properties.description:
Benny's Billiards and Sports Bar is a new pool hall and restaurant open in the Reedy Creek Square plaza in the heart of Cary, N.C.  

It is the place to shoot pool, play darts and have a few drinks but also a place to relax, enjoy a delicious full menu and enjoy conversation with all of your new friends and family.  Benny's features (10) 9-foot Brunswick pool tables for both rent and league play as well as in-house cash league.  There is a full bar with craft beer always on tap and top shelf liquors.  Whether it is drinks, pool, darts or food, Benny's has something for everyone.

properties.name: Berkeley Cafe
properties.description: Sadlack's Heroes and Berkeley Cafe have merged to reopen Berkeley Cafe. This live music venue and cafe have been in Raleigh since 1980 and features folk and rock music, popular food selections from each restaurant and an outdoor patio.

properties.name: Berto's Chimis
properties.description: Berto's Chimis is a food truck located at BaySix offering Dominican "chimi" burgers.f

properties.name: Bestow Baked Goods
properties.description: We're Bestow Baked Goods and we make desserts to mark special occasions. Whether it's a wedding, a birthday, a delicious start to your day or a "just because" treat--we make the moments that matter just a little bit sweeter.

properties.name: Bibibop Asian Grill
properties.description: Bibibop serves real, unprocessed, high quality Asian food because we believe that well-being can start with a good meal.

properties.name: Bida Manda
properties.description: Bida Manda is a thoughtful and sharp gathering place celebrating the diverse food traditions and culture of Laos. Bida Manda is the Sanskrit ceremonial term for father and mother and so named to honor the owners' parents in Laos who instilled their love of food and its power to bring people together. Located in the Moore Square district of downtown Raleigh, Bida Manda is one of the first Laotian restaurants in the U.S.

properties.name: Big Al's BBQ
properties.description: Slow roasted. Wood fired. Award-winning Carolina Smokin' Hot BBQ deliciousness.

properties.name: Big Dom's Bagel Shop
properties.description: Grab-and-go bagel shop in downtown Cary featuring hand rolled bagels, biscuits and b'donuts (baked donuts).

properties.name: Big Ed's City Market Restaurant
properties.description: Southern comfort and hospitality in a 170-seat restaurant displaying historical antiques/memorabilia of North Carolina.

properties.name: Big Ed's Garner
properties.description: Big Ed's Garner is proud to be the third restaurant in the Big Ed's family. Serving breakfast all-day and country cooking classics, we are a family-friendly environment where everyone and anyone can come together for a down home, freshly cooked meal.

properties.name: Big Ed's North
properties.description: This place was founded by Big Ed Watkins, who claims some of the recipes were handed down from his great-grandfather, a Confederate mess sergeant. Southern cooking doesn't get much more traditional than this place; make sure you indulge in the biscuits. The restaurant is filled with antique farm implements and political memorabilia, including snapshots of presidential candidates who have stopped by.

properties.name: Big Mikes BBQ
properties.description: Brew N Que is a retail and restaurant space for locally focused craft beer, and a brick and mortar home to Big Mikes BBQ (food truck and caterer). Big Mikes' full food truck menu is available for lunch each day through early evening and then the space converts over to a funky gastro pub that focuses on local farm-to-table ingredients. Craft beer is available for retail and draft beer consumption on-site. Growlers can be filled and taken home as well.

properties.name: Bigfoot Taphouse
properties.description: Bigfoot Taphouse is conveniently located on Glenwood South! Home of the Big"foot" Long, Bigfoot Taphouse is a family-owned restaurant with a wall of pour your own taps with a variety of Beer, wine, cocktails, and ciders to choose from.  Don't worry, if you don't feel like pouring your own, one of the friendly staff will grab you a cold one!  While enjoying a beverage, fill your belly with a gourmet hotdog, appetizer, or ice cream float!  The cozy atmosphere, convenience, and variety will have you coming back for more!

properties.name: Birdie's Barroom and Kitchen
properties.description:
When you pair LM Restaurants, a family-owned hospitality group whose been in the Triangle for over 45 years with Highwoods, one of the largest real estate groups in Raleigh, you get Birdie's Barroom & Kitchen.

"We believe that if we can stimulate talent at the start with a great cup of coffee, nourish it at noon with lunch and hydrate it at happy hour with a drink or two, they will keep coming back and be better together. "
- Brian Leary, Executive VP/COO, Highwoods

From the moment you step into Birdie's, you're enveloped in an atmosphere that feels both contemporary and welcoming. The design harmoniously blends modern aesthetics with colorful touches with floor-to-ceiling windows that offer breathtaking views of the city below. It's a space designed to foster connection, whether you're meeting friends for a casual lunch, enjoying a romantic dinner, or unwinding at the outside bar with colleagues after a long day.

properties.name: Biryani MAXX Indian Cuisine
properties.description: If Biryani is what you love, you have come to the best place to have it. Biryani MAXX Indian Cuisine's mission is to ensure that they serve the best Hyderabadi Dum Biryani, using the best ingredients possible, at an amazing price and quantity that will leave you more than satisfied. Plenty of tasty vegetarian dishes are available to bring completeness to the Indian cuisine.

properties.name: Bistro In The Park (Embassy Suites Raleigh-Durham/Research Triangle)
properties.description: Newly renovated the bar centric, relaxing atmosphere of Bistro in the Park welcomes any appetite with crisp salads, succulent soups to speciality pastas, steak and fresh seafood delicacies. Our community tables and open style kitchen featuring our pizza oven for chef inspired flatbreads make for an aromatic experience.  Have a small group of 12 or less, ask about our private dining room.

properties.name: Bittersweet
properties.description: Bittersweet is a terribly wonderful dessert, coffee and cocktail lounge with an all-natural, seasonal menu. They are a place where you can get bourbon with your pie, champagne with your cake and Irish whiskey in your coffee. The menu changes each season, with drink and dessert pairing specials offered regularly. They also have a full coffee and espresso menu—everything from cappuccinos to pourovers—with beans from Counter Culture Coffee in Durham.

properties.name: Blaze Pizza - Garner
properties.description: Exceptional quality at crazy fast speed is what Blaze Pizza is all about. Fresh, made-from-scratch dough. Healthful, artisan ingredients on the assembly line. Inventive to classic. You decide. Blazing hot oven + dedicated pizza-smith + 180 seconds = fast-fire'd, perfectly crisp perfection. Sound good? Enjoy the rest of your day.

properties.name: Blaze Pizza - Holly Springs
properties.description: Exceptional quality at crazy fast speed is what Blaze Pizza is all about. Fresh, made-from-scratch dough. Healthful, artisan ingredients on the assembly line.
