A downtown neighborhood reborn from its transportation and industrial roots, Smoky Hollow is a transformative, multiphase district developed in partnership with Williams Realty + Building Company that has redefined the Northern gateway to Downtown Raleigh. 

Smoky Hollow boasts a thoughtfully curated selection of establishments, catering to a diverse range of interests and tastes. Whether you're a beer enthusiast or looking for a sweet treat for your furry companion, this neighborhood has it all.

properties.name: Snooker's Billiards
properties.description: Get serious about pool, darts and suds.

properties.name: Social Club
properties.description: Bringing you a little piece of NYC to Raleigh, Glenwood Social Club is a lounge bar featuring some of the best drinks, stone oven pizza, and live music. Enjoy up and coming DJ's/performers while sipping on some of the best selected wines, handcrafted cocktails, or local beers.

properties.name: Sous Terre
properties.description:
Sous Terre is an intimate 1000-square foot underground bar with banquette and bar seating for 35 focuses on the classics – such as the legendary shaken-to-order Ramos Gin Fizz, famous French 75 with Cognac from Arnaud’s in New Orleans, a modern Paloma updated with mezcal and black salt, and the tiki style Cobra’s Fang with house made fassionola syrup and falernum. 

Keys to access Sous Terre can be purchased at Crawford and Sons or Jolie for $50 which gives you a lifetime membership. If you dine at one of their restaurants upstairs, you will not need a key to enjoy Sous Terre. Keys previously purchased for Atlantic lounge will work.

properties.name: Split Raleigh
properties.description: Split Raleigh is a luxury tequila lounge and live music burrow located in Glenwood South, Raleigh.

properties.name: Stella's
properties.description: “like if a dive bar were a girl”

properties.name: Stonewalls Tavern
properties.description: Stonewalls Tavern is a friendly neighborhood bar located on Hillsborough St. near N.C. State University.

properties.name: TJ's Night Life
properties.description: TJ's Night Life is home of RAYZ Deck Party and the Raleigh Shag Club! TJ's features live bands, DJ events, shag lessons and many special events throughout the year. Also host your private parties at TJ's!

properties.name: Teets
properties.description: Teets is a bar located at the heart of downtown's Glenwood South district, owned and operated by Bates Battaglia (former Carolina Hurricane) and Anthony Battaglia (former professional hockey player), and both Amazing Race 22 grand prize winners. With its massive front and back patio and over 40-ft.-long main bar inside, Teets has multiple TVs as well as a giant projection screen to watch your favorite hockey games as well as other sports. With its lounging atmosphere, pool table, corn hole and darts, it's a great place whether you want to unwind after work or are just getting started for a night on the town. An extensive drink selection and your favorite music, and lots to keep you entertained, while checking out some history as to how Teets came to be.

properties.name: The Architect Bar & Social House
properties.description: The Architect Bar & Social House is an original concept centered on a chic but casual atmosphere that features a beer list second to none and unique cocktail menu inspired by molecular mixology. They aim to create a warm and welcoming environment that includes live music Sunday through Saturday and late night dancing on the weekends.

properties.name: The Bison Bar
properties.description: Neighborhood friendly bar in North Raleigh with good people and good times. Open 4pm-2am daily, serving $2 PBR and Miller High Life every day of the week. Check out this local watering hole for UFC fights and stop by on Mondays for $1 domestic bottles.

properties.name: The Blind Barbour
properties.description: The Blind Barbour is a cozy neighborhood craft cocktail bar with almost 200 whiskeys, scotches and bourbons.

properties.name: The Bridge DTR
properties.description: The London Bridge Pub is a downtown Raleigh bar located in the heart of the entertainment district on E. Hargett St. They offer an eclectic range of beers and mixed drinks, as well as a very comfortable and massive outdoor patio with plenty of room to hang out or sit around and have a drink in the nice N.C. weather. London Bridge also provides a very enjoyable atmosphere inside to relax, meet new people, dance, network or to just watch soccer in downtown Raleigh. They are 100% pet friendly, so even your four legged friends can participate. Come join The London Bridge Pub on the weekend nights to party with a fantastic array of DJ's, music and time with your friends. Get get your weekends going at this Raleigh English pub.

properties.name: The Cardinal
properties.description: The Cardinal is just a cozy cabin-esque watering hole atop a hill with a large ‘dog friendly front patio’ overlooking Downtown Raleigh so please lower your expectations and stop on by for a ponder, drink and a taste, and if still interested, fill out a membership application and join the Cardinal family for a lifetime of “spirits & everybody” and hotdogs, of course. Inquire Within...

properties.name: The Green Light
properties.description: Behind a hidden door, off of a bustling street in downtown Raleigh, you’ll find The Green Light. The Green Light is a well-kept cocktail secret aimed to intrigue every taste ranging from the cocktail connoisseur to the curious wanderer. The Green Light is situated in a secret room, which lies in what was once an architect's office. Look for the bookcase door, walk into a cozy get-away and enjoy a second-to-none cocktail experience.

properties.name: The Haymaker
properties.description: The Haymaker is a cocktail bar in downtown Raleigh. Inspired by fighters and '90s rappers alike, The Haymaker brings you originals like “Sing Like a Bee” and “One-Two Combo.” Bring your friends and enjoy a knockout punch bowl, or try the featured bubbles on tap (really) for instant sparkles and happiness.

properties.name: The Hippo Wine Bar
properties.description: The Hippo is your neighborhood wine bar and shop, located in downtown Raleigh. We specialize in natural, low-intervention, and sustainable wines. Our staff can help you try something new or guide you to your familiar favorites.

properties.name: The Iron Oaks
properties.description:
Located in Sojourn Glenwood south of Crabtree. Enjoy over 36 drafts, 40 wines, and locally inspired drinks & tapas. Come play the back 9 & unwind!

Reserve our GolfZon Simulators for a high definition, luxury indoor golf experience. Golfers have full access to our bar and food menus.

properties.name: The Merchant
properties.description: The Merchant pays homage to a forgotten piece of Raleigh history. A vintage, secret door provides an escape to a cocktail experience nestled in classic atmosphere with modern flair. The Merchant will offer guests a carefully selected lineup of classic and adventurous cocktail options along with a chef-driven bar bites menu. Our aim is to elevate your drinking experience.

properties.name: The Parlor at Heights House
properties.description:
The Parlor at Heights House has a meticulously curated menu composed of Italian influenced craft cocktails, an all-Italian wine list & local beers – all in an effort to reflect & honor the Italianate style of this 1858 historic mansion. Charcuterie plates are also available. Guests are greeted by Heights House Hotel’s team and Raleigh native Will Bryant – manager and mixologist of The Parlor. Reservations via TOCK are required and can be made up to 30 days in advance. They allow for groups of up to 6 in a reservation. (Please note, overnight hotel guests are not required to make a reservation.) Upon arrival, Heights House Hotel welcomes guests to enter through the front door and order from the bar in the Parlor, and then explore this historic home’s common spaces – including Parlor, Drawing Room, Dining Room, Library and lower lounge – as well the two front terraces and fire pit on the front lawn, for seating. (Please park on the street and use the front entrance.)

Please note that Friday & Saturday evenings are reserved for overnight guests only.

properties.name: The Walk Up
properties.description: The Walk Up, in downtown Cary, is an upstairs cocktail bar offering a wide array of drink selections.

properties.name: Tonic, Bar & Social Club
properties.description: Tonic, Bar and Social Club is a top-shelf neighborhood bar featuring craft cocktails, beer, and wine.

properties.name: Tonic, Bar and Social Club
properties.description: Tonic, Bar and Social Club is a top-shelf neighborhood bar featuring craft cocktails, beer, and wine. Every Fri. and Sat. night, enjoy live music.

properties.name: Ugly Monkey
properties.description: Raleigh's self-acclaimed best party throwers. No cover - ever. Located in downtown Raleigh and open from 7pm-2am daily.

properties.name: Unwined on White
properties.description: Unwined on White is an upscale wine lounge and yoga studio featuring boutique wines and craft beer in the heart of historic Downtown Wake Forest, N.C.

properties.name: Vicious Fishes Taproom, Biergarten & Piranha Joe Coffee
properties.description: Vicious Fishes' Apex location offers a taproom and coffee shop. Vicious Fishes is a brewer of balanced and juicy IPAs, crisp, clean lagers and deliciously fruited sour beers.

properties.name: Vita Vite
properties.description:
An art gallery and wine bar located in the Warehouse District, Vita Vite Downtown invites guests to relax in a rustic, cozy ambience with plush fireside couches, a comfortable bar and an outdoor porch. Guests can savor a menu of internationally curated wines, craft beers, small plates and desserts while perusing artwork and goods from southern artists. Vita Vite Downtown’s 5,600 square foot space includes an event venue (1,200 square feet) that can host groups of up to 80 people. Or choose our intimate gallery space that holds up to 30 people and is the ideal atmosphere for a more casual event.
Owner Lindsay Rice opened Vita Vite as a way to blend her two passions - art and wine. She wanted to create a comfortable space to help people visualize the artwork in their homes - all while enjoying a glass of wine.

properties.name: Vita Vite Midtown
properties.description:
A wine bar and art gallery nestled in North Hills, Vita Vite Midtown features a menu of internationally curated wines along with craft beers on tap, small plates and locally sourced desserts. Guests can purchase art from southern artists as well as goods from specialty artisans and vendors. The 6,000-square foot space blends a modern, edgy ambience with a sophisticated charm, showcasing artful Moroccan tiles and found materials from a 150-year-old Virginian church. Marked by a 360-degree bar, the second-story mezzanine affords vistas of Midtown Park through a retractable glass wall.
Owner Lindsay Rice opened Vita Vite as a way to blend her two passions - art and wine. She wanted to create a comfortable space to help people visualize the artwork in their homes - all while enjoying a glass of wine.

properties.name: Whiskey Rose
properties.description: Whiskey Rose is a high volume country bar with a western twist located in downtown Raleigh.

properties.name: William & Company
properties.description: A cozy cocktail bar tucked in the heart of historic Oakwood. Come by for a unique selection of locally sourced, fresh and refreshing, yet inexpensive, drinks.

properties.name: Wolfe & Porter
properties.description: Wolfe & Porter is a cocktail bar and event space on West Morgan Street, right next to Raleigh’s iconic Irregardless Café. From the classics to our own unique craft cocktails, we challenge you to find a better drink in Raleigh. We developed this space with a focus on fresh, innovative ingredients and an elevated experience. With a curated beer and wine selection, craft cocktails, antique bourbons and more, we hope you’ll join us to watch your favorite game, listen to live music, or enjoy the outdoors on our front patio and back deck.

properties.name: Zenith Raleigh
properties.description: Zenith Raleigh is a pop culture themed bar featuring decor based on all your favorite celebrity icons and monumental happenings throughout history! A night of pulse pounding dancing with our live DJs or a relaxed afternoon enjoying great cocktails and talking with friends about your favorite fiction is what we have in store.

properties.name: Blown Away Raleigh
properties.description:
Blown Away, the ultimate blow dry bar experience, will leave you...well...blown away!


So what’s a blow dry bar, you ask? Take the best parts about going to a salon: the relaxing shampoo, the professional blow dry, the drop-dead gorgeous style, throw in a glass of champagne -- and voilà! (Everything but the cut and color.) In a fraction of the time and cost, you've got your salon look and are feeling fab! Located within the booming North Hills development in Raleigh's Midtown, just steps away from the trendiest boutiques, premier restaurants and exciting nightlife!

properties.name: JC Raulston Arboretum at North Carolina State University
properties.description: Internationally recognized as one of the premier collections of trees and shrubs, this stunning garden displays more than 6,000 different types of plants from around the world. Stroll through numerous themed gardens, extensive plant collections and more. Free admission. Hours: Daily, 8am-8pm (except Nov.-Mar., 8am-5pm).

properties.name: William B. Umstead State Park
properties.description: Stroll nature trails or walk along 22 miles of hiking trails meandering through forest. Also offered are camping, picnicking, canoe rentals, fishing, visitor center nature study and 13 miles of horseback-riding and mountain-biking trails. Free admission; fee for boat and facility rental. Hours: Daily, 8am-sunset approximately; call or visit website.

properties.name: Fuquay Mineral Spring Park
properties.description:
Visit the Fuquay Mineral Spring Park and drink the “healing waters” from the Fuquay Mineral Spring, for which the town gets the first part of its name. A beautiful place to picnic, walk and reflect. Fuquay Mineral Spring Park offers picnic tables, a brick walking path and restored spring house.
Photo: Chris Richman

properties.name: Art to Heart Corridor
properties.description: Beginning at the North Carolina Museum of Art (where parking and admission to the museum are free) and ending in downtown Raleigh, this 5.9-mile paved trail winds through the museum’s beautiful 164-acre park, passes behind Meredith College, cuts through the main campus at North Carolina State University, zips by Pullen Park and finishes in the heart of the city just outside of the Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts.

properties.name: Black Creek Greenway
properties.description: At 7.1 miles in length, the Black Creek Greenway is one of the Town of Cary's longest greenway trails. Beginning at the Old Reedy Creek Rd. trailhead overlooking Lake Crabtree (which has bathrooms and more than 80 parking spaces available), the trail moves south, passing through North Cary Park and ultimately reaching Fred G. Bond Metro Park (where it connects to the White Oak Creek Greenway for an additional 7+ miles moving west). The greenway is open to walkers, hikers, cyclists, leashed pets, children and other users from dawn to dusk.

properties.name: Mountains-to-Sea Trail
properties.description:
The Mountains-to-Sea Trail stretches 1,175 miles from Clingmans Dome in the Great Smoky Mountains to Jockey's Ridge on the Outer Banks. Today, more than 500 miles of footpath are built. With temporary connectors on back roads and state bike routes, people can now hike across the state.

Friends of the Mountains-to-Sea Trail's mission is to bring together communities and volunteers to build the Mountains-to-Sea Trail, a simple footpath connecting the state's natural treasures for the enjoyment and education of people.

properties.name: Neuse River Canoe Trail
properties.description: The Parks and Recreation Department provides five canoe launches along 17 miles of the Neuse River starting at the Falls Lake Dam. Gravel or dirt drives provide year-round access for putting in paddle-craft. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset. Call or visit website for maps.

properties.name: Neuse River Greenway Trail
properties.description: The Neuse River Greenway Trail—a 27.5-mile paved, uninterrupted greenway that stretches from Falls Lake in North Raleigh to the Wake County line in southeast Raleigh—is a year-round haven for outdoor recreation. With views of historical sites as well as winding boardwalk areas and suspension bridges crossing over wetlands, the trail is open to joggers, walkers, runners, cyclists, roller bladers and others. Many consider the Neuse River Greenway Trail to be the gem of the 100-plus-mile Capital Area Greenway System.

properties.name: White Oak Creek Greenway
properties.description: One of the most important greenway trails in the Town of Cary parks system, the White Oak Creek Greenway travels approximately 7.5 miles from east to west, connecting to Fred G. Bond Metro Park on one end, and the American Tobacco Trail on the other. The greenway is open to walkers, hikers, cyclists, leashed pets, children and other users from dawn to dusk.

properties.name: American Tobacco Trail
properties.description: The Wake County portion of the American Tobacco Trail is a recreational rail-trail open to walkers, runners, dog walkers, bicyclists and horseback riders. Environmental and cultural history programs are also offered. This rail-trail project spans 22 miles, from rural New Hill in western Wake County, through northeast Chatham County, to downtown Durham, near the Durham Bulls Athletic Park.

properties.name: Annie Louise Wilkerson, MD, Nature Preserve
properties.description:
The City of Raleigh received an amazing gift of 157 acres of land along Falls Lake to create its first designated nature preserve in February 2006. Dr. Annie Louise Wilkerson, a renowned Raleigh doctor with many pioneering achievements in her 53-year career in medicine, stipulated in her will that the park be maintained as a "nature preserve park" used for the primary purpose of nature and wildlife education.

Three loop trails have been created on the 157-acre property. In addition, the Mountains-to-Sea Connector links the preserve’s trails with the Mountain-to-Sea Trail that follows the south shore of Falls Lake.

properties.name: Apex Community Park
properties.description:
The cornerstone of the Apex Parks system is the 160-acre Community Park. The park includes picnic shelters, playground, fishing lake, restroom facilities, nature and fitness trails and various athletic fields. The 50+ acre lake allows fishing with a permit from the town, and is available for use by canoes, kayaks, john boats (not exceeding 14 ft in length) and rowing skulls if launched at the designated area.


Step up your fitness at the Elevate Fitness Course at Apex Community Park (near the back tennis courts). Wear comfortable clothes and athletic shoes to try out the equipment, inspired by the fast-growing trend of obstacle course fitness.

properties.name: Apex Nature Park
properties.description: Apex Nature Park offers amenities such as an amphitheatre, disc golf course, multi-use trails, a dog park, multi-age playground, picnic shelter with restrooms and lighted tennis courts and soccer/multi-use fields. Free concerts and movies offered during the summer at the amphitheatre. Visit website for event dates and times.

properties.name: Bailey and Sarah Williamson Preserve
properties.description:
Triangle Land Conservancy’s 405-acre Bailey and Sarah Williamson Preserve offers more than seven miles of walking and biking trails that wind through forests and fields and connect to the Neuse River Greenway. It is TLC’s first public preserve to have working farms on site, and TLC’s vision is that one day, people will be able to walk or bike through the preserve and leave with fresh produce purchased from farmers who work on the land.
What to know before visiting Williamson Preserve:

Preserve hours are dawn to dusk, but it will be closed after rain to protect the trails and prevent run-off into streams. Check trail status before you go at trianglemtb.com, at torc-nc.org and on TLC's Facebook page.
Trails can be accessed via the Neuse River Greenway or at the parking lot at 4409 Mial Plantation Rd. The closest greenway parking lot is 6090 Mial Plantation Rd., Raleigh 27610
Most trails at Williamson Preserve go in one direction. On Sun.-Wed., walkers should turn right at trail intersections, and bikers turn left. On Thurs.-Sat., walkers turn left, and bikers turn right.
Dogs must be on leash at all times for their safety and the safety of other visitors, wildlife and livestock.
Do not interact with wildlife or livestock, and do not touch or approach any farm equipment or buildings.
Please take all trash, including dog poop bags, with you when you leave.
Full rules and a map are online.

properties.name: Blue Jay Point County Park
properties.description: Located on the shores of Falls Lake in northern Wake County, the 236-acre park's mission of environmental education is accomplished through exhibits, demonstration areas and educational programming. The park also offers picnicking, hiking trails, open play fields, playgrounds and a Go Ape TreeTop Adventure Course. Park admission is free and hours are 8am-sunset, daily.

properties.name: Carl Alwin Schenck Memorial Forest
properties.description: The Carl Alwin Schenck Memorial Forest is a 245 acre forest located in western Wake County about 10 minutes from the NC State campus. It is managed by N.C. State as a teaching and research forest to demonstrate the multiple benefits generated by an actively-managed forest. Visitors can walk the well-maintained trails to enjoy bird-watching and wildlife, see a managed forest that shows successional stages and enjoy the well-maintained picnic facilities. The Frances L. Liles Trail is most frequently used by the public. This trail passes through a number of sites where a variety of management practices are being employed, including those to support different wildlife habitats and encourage specific plants and animals.

properties.name: Carroll Howard Johnson Environmental Education Park
properties.description:
Get back to nature at the Carroll Howard Johnson Environmental Education Park.  Explore the 2 mile nature trail and uncover the natural treasures in Fuquay-Varina.  Crossing beautiful overlooks and natural bridges, visitors will find a path of wooded splendor, local flora and fauna and many species of birds that highlight the everyday wonders of Fuquay-Varina’s nature.

Facilities include two miles of interpretive walking trails, overlooks, bridges, amphitheater, picnic shelter and restrooms.

properties.name: Centennial Park
properties.description: This beautiful park features soccer fields, picnic shelter and .36 miles of paved walking trails. The shelter is available for rental and can seat 50 people. Centennial Park is used as part of the CASL National Soccer Series program and is one of their 13 venues.

properties.name: Crowder County Park
properties.description: Offers visitors opportunities to enjoy nature, walk, picnic, play or participate in an environmental education program. Includes a 2.7-acre pond with a boardwalk and observation decks (no fishing), three picnic shelters, three playgrounds, 0.8-mile, paved, accessible trail, amphitheater, educational gardens, play field and sand volleyball. Free admission. Hours: Daily, 8am-sunset.

properties.name: Durant Nature Preserve
properties.description: This 237-acre nature preserve offers five miles of trails, a playground, picnic areas, nature activities and rental facilities. Program and rental information available by calling the park office. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: E. Carroll Joyner Park
properties.description: The 117-acre E. Carroll Joyner Park features restored farm buildings, a pecan grove, 1,000 lawn-seat amphitheater, walker garden, a performance garden, 2,000 linear foot stone ribbon wall, three miles of paved walking trails and charcoal grills.

properties.name: Forest Ridge Park
properties.description:
Forest Ridge Park is 587 acres of parkland adjacent to Falls Lake with mountain biking, multi-use trails, fishing, wildlife garden, and nature programs. Get up-to-date information on what Forest Ridge has to offer by visiting their Welcome Center.

Forest Ridge Park has 2 accessible parking spaces located in the parking lot in front of the welcome center and 4 accessible parking spaces at the playground and shelter area.

properties.name: Garner Recreational Park
properties.description: Garner Recreational Park is located in the Historic Garner District. This park features two ball fields, a playground and 2.25 miles of mountain biking trails. In the Creech Rd. section of the park, at 190 Creech Rd., there are lighted tennis courts. Please call to reserve athletic fields.

properties.name: Green Hills County Park
properties.description: A day at North Wake Landfill District Park provides a variety of recreational activities for all ages. The park  includes a playground, trail access, picnic shelter and restrooms facilities.

properties.name: Hemlock Bluffs Nature Preserve/Stevens Nature Center
properties.description: Hemlock Bluffs Nature Preserve is a unique, 140-acre preserve featuring approximately three miles of trails, unique vegetation and Eastern Hemlock trees. Interactive nature programs are conducted at the Stevens Nature Center. Free admission (fee for some programs). Hours vary; call or visit website.

properties.name: Horseshoe Farm Nature Preserve
properties.description:
Carved out by the meandering of the Neuse River, Horseshoe Farm Nature Preserve sits on a U-shaped piece of land in northeastern Wake County with exceptional natural and cultural resources. The Preserve is a jewel along the Neuse River; a place of great natural beauty, abundant wildlife and rich heritage.


Surrounded on three sides by the Neuse River, Horseshoe Farm Nature Preserve consists of primarily undeveloped pastures and woodland areas. A natural surface trail runs along the wood line of the preserve for approximately 0.5 miles. A paved connector trail leads to the Neuse River section of the greenway from the Preserve's restroom building.

properties.name: Jones Park
properties.description: Jones Park includes playgrounds, a fishing pond, trails and a baseball/softball facility that was developed through partnerships with the Wake County Public School System and Wake County. Jones Park also offers an 18-hole disc-golf course.

properties.name: Knightdale Environmental Education Park
properties.description:
Knightdale Environmental Education Park is located behind Knightdale Town Hall on Steeple Square Ct. The park offers a 1/3 mile walking trail, picnic shelters, four environmental sculptures and two observation overlooks. The park can be accessed by parking on the side lot of Knightdale Town Hall or by parking at the rear of the East Regional Library parking lot.
Photo via the Town of Knightdale

properties.name: Kelly Road Park
properties.description: Kelly Road Park consists of 25 acres, including the Kidstown Playground. This Apex park also includes a picnic shelter with grill, baseball field, tennis courts and Trailhead Beaver Creek Greenway. Open 7am-10pm (March-Oct.) and 7am-8pm (Nov.-Feb.).

properties.name: Knightdale Station Park
properties.description: Knightdale Station is a 76-acre park in eastern Wake County. It includes two miles of paved trails, picnic shelters, the Ashley Wilder Dog Park, athletic fields, restrooms and a large playground. The playground is farm- and train-themed to serve as a reminder of Knightdale's agriculture and railroad past. Open daily from dawn until dusk.

properties.name: Lake Lynn Park and Community Center
properties.description: Lake Lynn Park has a 2.8 mile greenway trail around Lake Lynn, a batting cage, four tennis courts, two bocce courts, a youth baseball field and a playground. The Lake Lynn Community Center includes a gymnasium with basketball courts, meeting room, art room, dance studio and warming kitchen.

properties.name: Main Street Park
properties.description:
Main Street Park has two entrances one at 200 South Main St. and 500 Scarboro St. Main Street Park has four rentable shelters, a gazebo, open play field, play ground and over one mile of greenway trails.
Photo via the Town of Rolesville

properties.name: Marla Dorrel Park
properties.description: Home of the Kids Together Playground, Marla Dorrel Park isn’t your typical suburban park. Unique elements include a dragon climbing structure named Katal, progressive design elements and landscaping, and a play area where kids of all physical and mental ability can enjoy fully-integrated play in a multi-sensory environment that challenges both muscles and minds. The park connects to a pedestrian overpass linking it to MacDonald Woods Park. The trail crosses a stream that runs adjacent to the park and a small wetland can be found close by.

properties.name: Mill Bridge Nature Park
properties.description: Mill Bridge Nature Park has a 200-seat amphitheater along with greenway trails that currently connect with the Wake Forest Parks and Recreation greenways. The town has future plans to connect with the current greenway tails at Main Street Park.

properties.name: Mingo Creek Park & Trails
properties.description:
Mingo Creek Park is located on an 8.2-acre site. The Mingo Creek Trail follows the course of Mingo Creek from its confluence with the Neuse River near Raleigh's Anderson Point Park up to Mingo Creek Park adjacent to the Timber Ridge subdivision off Laurens Way. Along the way, the trail features connections into the Princeton Manor, Planter's Walk and Carrington Woods subdivisions.
Photo via the Town of Knightdale

properties.name: River Bend Park
properties.description:
River Bend Park includes parking, restrooms, a playground, a kayak loading/unloading area, a kayak launch, and access to the Neuse River Greenway.

The 25-acre park has playgrounds with a rubberized safety surface designed for children ages 2-5 years old and 5-12 years old that feature a multi-direction swing, slides, and a climbing boulder.

River Bend Park is one of several launch sites on the Neuse River for small non-motorized crafts, including canoes and kayaks. The park provides general parking and kayak or canoe trailer parking, as well as a designated unloading/loading area near the launch.

The Neuse River Greenway trail runs through River Bend Park.

properties.name: Robert V. Godbold Park
properties.description: Robert V. Godbold Park is like multiple parks in one! Its amenities include six tennis courts (lighted) available on a first-come, first serve basis when not being utilized by a Town of Cary program, and are free of charge, two lighted basketball slabs, a playground, picnic tables, restrooms,  trail with exercise stations and dog park (Passes can be purchased for this off-leash dog park at any of the Town's community centers. The passes are valid for Jack Smith Park and Godbold Dog Park). Robert V. Godbold Park is also home to Sk8-Cary Skate Park.

properties.name: Robertson Millpond Preserve
properties.description: Located just east of Raleigh in the town of Wendell, Robertson Millpond Preserve is a hidden 85-acre refuge for nature lovers, canoeists and kayakers. Opened to the public in 2015, the blackwater swamp property is the only bald cypress habitat in the Raleigh area, creating the unique experience of paddling through a forest-like setting. Open on weekends and some holidays, the preserve's 1.15-mile loop paddling trail (marked by more than 70 buoys) is the main draw for canoists and kayakers. On Saturdays from April-Oct., Paddle Creek, a private rental and guide company, has solo and tandem kayaks available for hourly rentals. A parking and launch area allows you to bring your own canoe or kayak as well for no fee.

properties.name: Sandy Pines Preserve
properties.description: Sandy Pines Preserve offers a picnic area, hiking, walking and horse-back trails, as well as fishing. This 563-acre preserve of forests and fields is the largest single tract of land owned by Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space.

properties.name: Shelley Lake Park
properties.description: This 53-acre lake and park provides two miles of paved, scenic greenway trails with exercise workout stations. Visitors may enjoy fishing, biking, hiking and picnicking. Free admission. Hours: Daily, sunrise-sunset.

properties.name: South Garner Park
properties.description: The park features three softball fields, a multipurpose field, tennis courts, a hiking trail and a large playground.

properties.name: South Park
properties.description: South Park, located in Fuquay-Varina, is a large multi-use park adjacent to the Fuquay-Varina Communtiy Center. The park includes a 6,000 square foot pentagon shaped splash pad (open daily through Labor Day, 11am-7pm) and access Jeff Wells Memorial Trail, a .7 mile greenway. It also has three youth softball/baseball fields, two multi-purpose fields, a picnic shelter, playground, walking track and restrooms.

properties.name: Veterans Park
properties.description: Veterans Park is dedicated to the men and women who have served our country in the military. The park features a liberty elm donated by the Elm Research Institute of Keene, N.H. as an enduring symbol of freedom. The park also includes a 4.3-acre pond, picnic shelter, playground, fitness stations, half-mile paved trail extending around the pond and a paved trail between Veterans Park and Jones Park.

properties.name: White Deer Park
properties.description: At 96 acres, White Deer Park is the largest municipal park in Garner. The park features two miles of paved trails, two playgrounds, five shelters, an arboretum and a 2,500-square-foot nature center. The park hosts special events like Groundhog Day and Trick-or-Treat the Trails. The Nature Center is used for the Town’s educational nature programming and is available for private rental. White Deer Park is open sunrise to sunset.

properties.name: A.J. Fletcher Opera Theater at Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts
properties.description: Fletcher Opera Theater, located on the east side of Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts, is the 600-seat theater designed for opera performances, dance, music and theatrical productions in an intimate setting.

properties.name: Arts Together
properties.description: Arts Together is Raleigh's only non-profit multi-arts school. Arts Together offers a rich blend of classes in art, dance, drama, voice, Pilates and yoga for ages 3 through 18 and adults. Arts Together offers a daily preschool designed around the arts as the basis for kindergarten readiness. As Raleigh's community school for the arts, Arts Together also has the distinction of nurturing the only area dance program focusing its curriculum around modern dance, with offerings for preschoolers through dance professionals. Located just shy of downtown Raleigh on Saint Mary's St., it is conveniently situated less than a block from Hillsborough St. and across from Saint Mary.s School.

properties.name: Black Box Dance Theatre
properties.description: Black Box Dance Theatre's mission is to celebrate local and global communities through non-fiction dance. This non-profit organization creates dances in Raleigh and beyond.

properties.name: Carolina Ballet, Inc.
properties.description: Carolina Ballet is an internationally-acclaimed professional ballet company based in Raleigh. Join the company for a season of classical favorites and world premieres, and experience the artistry, passion and beauty of world-class American ballet. Admission and locations vary; call 919.719.0900 or visit carolinaballet.com.

properties.name: Cary Academy Fine & Performing Arts Center
properties.description: Theater experiences at Cary Academy are rooted in and fueled by the ensemble ethic - the belief that we are a diverse group of people working together as one toward a common goal. The curriculum stresses self-exploration and discovery, while instilling within students a respect for the art and the artist and providing students with tools they may use to unleash their passion, their creativity, and their unique voice.

properties.name: Cary Ballet Company
properties.description: As an affiliate of the Cary Ballet Conservatory, Cary Ballet Company provides advanced level, pre-professional students the highest quality training and performing experience, as they progress into the next phase of their careers. The company produces several major performances annually, including Visions of Sugarplums, "Celebration of Children in the Arts" and their Spring Gala, which have become favorite traditions for our capital region audiences.

properties.name: Chamber Music Raleigh
properties.description: Now in its 79th Season, CMR is responsible for producing the chamber music concert series at the North Carolina Museum of Art and an annual gala event at the Governor’s Mansion. K-12 public music education & master class programming available.

properties.name: City Plaza
properties.description: City Plaza is located in the heart of the center city and features four glass retail pavilions, complimentary Wi-Fi, 50-foot programmable light towers and sculptures from N.C.-based artists. It’s where celebrations and civic pride are demonstrated year-round. Also, find the Raleigh, N.C., Visitor Information Center just off City Plaza, between the Raleigh Marriott City Center and the Raleigh Convention Center.

properties.name: Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek
properties.description: Raleigh’s premier open-air music venue showcases award-winning artists in an outdoor setting. Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek is the place to see the biggest concert superstars in the world as they tour the Southeast. Visit website for concert tickets, more venue details and event information. Box Office Hours: Mon.-Fri., 10am-4pm.

properties.name: Garner Performing Arts Center
properties.description: The Garner Performing Arts Center is a wonderful venue to host or attend a special event. The renovated auditorium offers 12,673 sq. ft. of space, which includes a versatile stage with fly space and rails, separate dressing rooms with restrooms, green room, loading dock, technician’s booth, updated lighting equipment and controls. The auditorium includes 465 comfortable, theater-style seats and meets all ADA requirements with easy wheelchair accessibility and seating. For more intimate gatherings, the auditorium’s beautifully decorated main lobby and back stage lobby can each provide a backdrop to celebrate any special occasion. A piano, podium, limited number of tables and folding chairs as well as a concession booth off the main lobby may be used for a additional charge. The venue is accessible via several major highways and there is plenty of free off street parking.

properties.name: Jones Auditorium at Meredith College
properties.description: Jones Auditorium has a proscenium theatre that seats 400 patrons downstairs and 220 in the balcony. Many dance and theatre productions are held in Jones Auditorium, which also hosts Meredith's lecture series and other special events each semester. Built in 1949, the auditorium was renovated in 1973 and had another facelift in the summer of 2008. The auditorium was named in honor of former trustees Wesley Norwood Jones and Sallie Bailey Jones.

properties.name: Joseph M. Bryan Jr. Theater in the Museum Park (N.C. Museum of Art)
properties.description: This unique performing arts and film venue—a work of art in itself—hosts an outdoor summer series featuring a range of musical performances, family entertainment, blockbuster movies and classic films. Picnics welcome; food and beverages available for purchase. Box Office Hours: Tues.-Thurs., 10am-5pm; Fri., 10am-9pm; Sat.-Sun., 10am-5pm.

properties.name: Kenan Recital Hall at William Peace University
Lincoln Theatre
properties.description: The Lincoln Theatre features some of the best national and regional touring acts along with great tribute and local artists. As one of Raleigh's best spots for live music, there is ample parking and all shows are general admission (unless otherwise noted). State of the art sound and light systems enhance the great music selection even more. Visit website for a list of upcoming shows.

properties.name: Lorraine's Coffee House and Music
properties.description: Lorraine's Coffee House is located in Garner. On various nights of the week, they have live bluegrass and acoustic music. The live music typically consists of bluegrass on Thursday nights, acoustic music on Friday nights and jazz/soft rock on Saturday nights. Visit website for full list of events and music schedule.

properties.name: Memorial Auditorium at Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts
properties.description: Opened in 1932, and renovated most recently in 2016, Memorial Auditorium is the crown jewel of N.C. performing arts. Over the years, this richly historic theater has played host to a dazzling spectrum of artists and performances. Just a sample of the list quickly becomes dizzying: Sinatra, Gillespie, Baryshnikov, Tony Bennett, Ray Charles, Sarah Vaughn, Itzhak Perlman, Natalie Cole and Prince. Broadway blockbusters like Les Misérables, The Phantom of the Opera, Disney’s The Lion King, Jersey Boys, Miss Saigon and Rent have also been staged here. Eighty-thousand square feet of stage, house, rehearsal hall, lobbies and public areas make Memorial Auditorium one of the most decisively versatile facilities in the Southeast.

properties.name: Meymandi Concert Hall at Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts
properties.description: The North Carolina Symphony calls this remarkable, 1750-seat venue home. And it’s easy to see why. Its 65-ft ceiling, unique shoe box shape, narrow sides, shallow balconies and lack of proscenium all work together to deliver the warmest, clearest and most immersive sound experience possible. National and international artists and performers now speak of this hall’s remarkable acoustics.

properties.name: Moonlight Stage Company
properties.description: Moonlight Stage Company is a black-box theatre dedicated to new works. Its priority is audiences, patrons, performers, writers and students. Performance areas include theatre, improv, original music, stand-up comedy, and writer's theatre. This company is also dedicated to its students in helping foster opportunities in performance and preparing them for the professional world of performing arts, specifically in theatre, film, television and music.

properties.name: North Carolina Master Chorale
properties.description: Bringing the very best in choral music performance to Raleigh—area audiences and presenting concerts of choral-orchestral masterworks. Under the direction of Alfred E. Sturgis, the nearly 200 voices of the chorale perform repertoire from the Renaissance to contemporary. $17-$38 admission; performance locations vary.

properties.name: North Carolina Opera
properties.description: The region’s professional opera company dedicated to presenting live, operatic performances accompanied by orchestra in staged productions with sets and costumes. The company engages international-level artists and the best in regional talent: it also presents special events and education programs. Admission varies; call or visit website.

properties.name: North Raleigh Arts & Creative Theatre
properties.description: NRACT is a non-profit, community-based performing arts center, created to enrich the cultural life of the North Raleigh community. A creative outlet is provided for all ages and NRACT openly invites community involvement. Along with providing instruction in the performing arts, NRACT seeks to promote the traditions and values of the theatre and to produce quality entertainment in a community-oriented atmosphere.

properties.name: PineCone, Piedmont Council of Traditional Music
properties.description: PineCone presents 30+ concerts per year, plus produces the annual IBMA Bluegrass Live! powered by PNC festival with IBMA and the City of Raleigh. Overall, PineCone presents more than 200 music programs each year, including concerts, youth programs, participatory jams and sessions, a weekly radio show, and more.

properties.name: Price Music Center at North Carolina State University
Raleigh Civic Symphony and Chamber Orchestra
properties.description: These orchestras combine student and community musicians with professional leaders and innovative programming in what has been called “a class act” and “bright lights on the music scene in Raleigh.” Admission and locations vary; call or visit website.

properties.name: Raleigh Dance Theatre
properties.description: Mary LeGere, Artistic Director, announces the 25th anniversary season of Raleigh Dance Theatre (RDT).  Raleigh Dance Theatre, affiliate company of the Raleigh School of Ballet, was founded in 1984 by Ann Vorus to provide pre-professional performance training, while promoting and fostering the art of dance in the community. It is an honor member company of Regional Dance America/Southeastern Regional Ballet Association.  RDT’s training program has a proven record of success, with alumnae who have gone on to professional careers with Carolina Ballet, Pennsylvania Ballet, Stuttgart Ballet, Washington Ballet II, and New York City Ballet among others. Our Spring Repertoire is March 20, 2010 at 2:00 and 7:00, with our 7:00 performance being a special Gala performance featuring several RDT alumni who are now dancing professionally.

properties.name: Raleigh Little Theatre
properties.description: There’s something for everyone at one of the nation’s longest- running community theatres, since 1936, including high- stepping musicals, outrageous comedies, dramas and family favorites. Recipient of 10 Best of the Triangle awards from the Indy and youth theater awards. $8-$30 admission. Box Office Hours: Mon.-Fri., noon-5pm.

properties.name: Raleigh Symphony Orchestra
properties.description: For more than 35 years, RSO has offered classical, chamber and family programs performed throughout the Raleigh area. In 1991, RSO was awarded the Raleigh Medal of Arts for its inclusive and innovative programming, community outreach and high artistic standards. Admission and locations vary; call or visit website.

properties.name: Red Hat Amphitheater
properties.description:
Red Hat Amphitheater is a GBAC STAR™ accredited 5,990-seat open-air amphitheater in the heart of Downtown Raleigh. Owned and operated by the City of Raleigh, the amphitheater belongs to The Complex, the City’s premier portfolio of convention and entertainment venues, which also includes the Raleigh Convention Center, Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts, and Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek.


Just steps from the fun and energy of downtown Raleigh’s bars, clubs, galleries and restaurants, Red Hat Amphitheater offers an immersive entertainment experience with stunning views of the Raleigh skyline.


Each season, live music fans continually look forward to a lineup of some of the hottest summer concerts spanning across a variety of genres. Built in 2010, more than 400 performers have played the amphitheater over the past 14 years. Alt-J, Bob Dylan, Imagine Dragons, John Legend, Kendrick Lamar, Tyler Childers, and Widespread Panic are among the artists who have graced the venue’s stage.

properties.name: Sertoma Amphitheatre
properties.description: Sertoma Amphitheatre, located between the Kiwanis Picnic Shelter and Bond Lake on a natural site at Fred G. Bond Metro Park, is one of Cary’s best-kept secrets. This intimate venue is a perfect setting for spring, summer and fall concerts. Come early for a seat, or pack your own portable chair. Concerts are free.

properties.name: Stewart Theatre, Talley Student Center at North Carolina State University
properties.description: Stewart Theatre is located on the second floor of the Talley Student Center on North Carolina State University's campus. The theatre seats 800. It is operated by staff with University Theatre and has offices on the first floor of Talley at 1202A. The theatre is used by campus organizations and student groups. It is available for rental use by outside organizations on a limited basis.

properties.name: Studio Theatre, Jones Hall at Meredith College
The Cornerstone
properties.description: The Cornerstone Convention Center is a state-of-the-art performance facility hosting private events, music, comedy and more. Spacious and comfortable seating, clean and safe environment, excellent customer service and professional audiovisual production make The Cornerstone experience memorable.

properties.name: The Halle Cultural Arts Center
properties.description: The Halle Cultural Arts Center hosts a number of premier performances, visual art exhibitions, and movies. Children and adult drama, voice, dance, art, and STEAM classes are also offered. Exquisitely revitalized in 2008, this architectural jewel is the perfect setting for your next reception, wedding, meeting or performance.

properties.name: The Piano Room
properties.description: The Piano Room is downtown Zebulon’s first Jazz Piano Lounge! Join us for our monthly concerts, wine events, poetry nights and music lessons!

properties.name: The Ritz
properties.description: The revitalized Ritz is an exciting event venue in Raleigh! With an artistic legacy that is rooted in rock 'n' roll, an extensive renovation and a commitment to creating a memorable guest experience, The Ritz is positioned to become a legendary venue. This one-of-a-kind, 12,000-square-foot venue has a state-of-the-art sound and lighting system, a well-trained, professional staff and a newly completed Stella Artois VIP Lounge designed by local N.C. artists. The remodeled black, white and “Ritz Red” interiors are the perfect blend of rock 'n' roll and elegance—classic in design but still hip and unique.

properties.name: The Wake Forest Listening Room
properties.description:
The Wake Forest Listening Room was started in 2017 as a series of performances around town featuring local and regional original musicians. The main intent of the WFLR is to give artists a “sacred space” where their music could be focused on with no distractions like sports on TVs, conversations, etc. It also provides the same for audience members.

The series found a permanent home downstairs from Sugar Magnolia Café, where we hosted more than 300 performances before COVID shut us down in late 2021.

In October 2023, we’re reopening in the new space next door to our independent Wake Forest bookstore, Page 158 Books. We’ll have more seating, new sound and light systems, delicious food and drinks, and we’ll keep that same “listening room” vibe that guests and musicians have come to love and appreciate!

All our shows and ticket links can be found on this site or at eTix.com. Join us for a show and enjoy a great evening of live, original music from some of the best local, regional, national and international artists!

properties.name: The Wicked Witch
properties.description: A bigger, nastier venue brought to you by the fine folks behind Raleigh's fave queer space Ruby Deluxe!

properties.name: Theatre In The Park
properties.description: As one of the state’s most innovative and exciting theatre arts centers, Theatre In The Park presents a wide range of comedy, contemporary drama, musicals, original works and Shakespeare in the theatre’s flexible, indoor performance space. Admission varies; call or visit website. Box Office Hours: Mon.-Fri., 9am-5pm.

properties.name: Thompson Hall at North Carolina State University
properties.description: Thompson Hall occupies The Crafts Center, teaching space, green room and two theatres on the campus of North Carolina State University.

properties.name: Tin Roof Raleigh
properties.description:
Tin Roof, A Live Music Joint, is about giving musicians a place to play and a place to hang when they aren't onstage.  The tasty food, fun, eclectic environment, community of Regulars, and friendly Crew have established the Roof as the place to be for musicians and non-musicans alike. Over the years, our stages have hosted the famous, the should have been famous, and everyone in between!

Located in Glenwood South featuring a first floor stage for live music, southern inspired 'Better Than Bar Food' & a second level with a rooftop patio! 

Whether you're coming for the tunes, the food, the drinks or just a good time, enjoy the Roof 'Where Everybody is Somebody'! Support live music and the musicians that bring it to us, and we'll hope to see ya enough to call you a Regular!

properties.name: Titmus Theatre
properties.description: Titmus Theatre is one of two theaters in Thompson Hall at North Carolina State University.

properties.name: Towne Players of Garner
properties.description:
The Towne Players was formed in 1998 as a means of increasing the awareness of the performing arts in Garner and Wake County. Run by a governing board made up of citizens from Garner, North Carolina and the greater Triangle area, the Towne Players produce four theatrical plays each year and offer theatre classes for children. As a community theatre, we depend upon many people who enjoy the beauty and sense of community that an organization can bring.

Formed in 1998 as a means of increasing the awareness of performing arts in Garner and Wake County, the Towne Players produce four theatrical plays each year and offer theatre classes for children. Recent accolades for the group have included being named the best community theatre in the Triangle area by Robert’s Reviews in 2002 and 2004.

properties.name: Triangle Wind Ensemble
properties.description: The Triangle Wind Ensemble is an adult wind ensemble based in North Carolina's Triangle region. Since 1999, many of the area's most talented wind and percussion players have joined together weekly to practice and perform an exciting range of music for audiences in both formal and informal settings. We aim to build community through music and to enrich the cultural lives of our musicians and audience members.

properties.name: William Peace Theatre
properties.description: Enjoy the arts this season at William Peace University (WPU)! Leggett Theatre is the University’s small theatre located on the second floor of the historic Main Building and seats 80. The Theatre is home to the William Peace Theatre Company and is available for outside bookings. Throughout the academic year, plays, musicals, concerts and other productions are held in Leggett Theatre. William Peace Theatre plays and musical productions begin at 7:30pm. Tickets are $5/$10/$15 for the 2014-15 academic year. Master classes, speaking events and other performances will vary. Music concerts, visiting lectures and other performances are held in Kenan Recital Hall at 7:30pm, with several free of charge. Visit the WPU website for up-to-date information, event times and locations.

properties.name: MacNair's Country Acres
properties.description: One of the Triangle's oldest privately owned riding academies, MacNair's has evolved into a full service riding facility. They offer lessons through a riding school for children and adults. Lessons are offered Monday through Saturday in the Community Program for students 10 years of age and older. The  Pony School is specially designed for young riders ages 6 through 10 years. Additional riding and educational opportunities are available for actively enrolled students through the clinic, club and horse show programs. Lighted rings and an indoor facility make it possible for lessons to continue through the year in almost any weather conditions. Come ride with MacNair's!

properties.name: Triangle Farms
properties.description: Triangle Farms, Inc., specializes in on-site horse show management services for both indoor and outdoor N.C. horse shows. Featuring hunter and jumper events, schooling shows and a wide range of equestrian breeds, Triangle Farms-managed horse shows run seamlessly and offer a professional, fun and safe environment for your family and horses to compete.

properties.name: 311 Gallery
properties.description: New juried or invited-artist show in the Main Gallery opening the First Friday of each month. Twelve working or exhibition studios include the works of over 30 resident artists, including abstract, landscape and portrait painters, photographers, potters and other artists.

properties.name: ARTS Wake Forest
properties.description: Wake Forest ARTS strives to support local artists and existing art programs throughout the Wake Forest community to encourage the formation of new arts ventures. Wake Forest ARTS meets the second Thursday of each month at 7:30 a.m. at an office in the Wake Forest Historical Museum, 450 N. Main St., Wake Forest, NC‎ 27587. Meetings are open to the public. Wake Forest ARTS office is open by appointment only at 901 Barnford Mill Road (984-235-7673).

properties.name: Alia Fine Art Studios
properties.description: Alia Fine Art Studios (AFAS) is a beautiful, teaching studio in Raleigh that helps students of all levels gain skills in drawing and painting the human figure and portrait. You will learn classical methods through a contemporary approach to representational figurative art. AFAS offers monthly classes, one day intensives and nationally acclaimed invited artist and expert workshops. For more info on current offerings, visit the "Classes" tab on the website. AFAS is located at Anchorlight in south Raleigh. Open Mon.-Fri. and by appointment. Please call ahead in case a class is in session.

properties.name: Anchorlight
properties.description:
Anchorlight is a creative space, founded with the intent of fostering artists at varying stages of their development. Anchorlight provides a combination of artist studios, residency opportunities, and exhibition space. Through the establishment of an internal community of artists, designers, and craftspeople, Anchorlight encourages mentorship and the cross-pollination of knowledge and skills. 

Anchorlight is by appointment only with the exception of special events. Gallery hours differ with each exhibition. See home page for current exhibition information and link for scheduling and event hours/times.

properties.name: Antfarm Studios
properties.description: Antfarm is home to a diverse group of artists working in a variety of media (metal, wood, clay, print, paint, drawing, fiber and more) who strive to create exceptional work and share it with the community. Antfarm was born in 1993 by a group of NC State College of Design school students. The original artists secured and renovated a 1925 warehouse located in Raleigh's historic Boylan Heights neighborhood. Acting as an evolving space, Antfarm has hosted over 40 artists and craftspeople in 10 individual studios since its inception. Antfarm strives to create exceptional work and share it with the community.

properties.name: Art by Shalimar
properties.description: Art by Shalimar is a studio and gallery independently owned and operated by the artist, Shalimar Waffa. She does not display prints or giclées; all paintings she sells are 100% original and unique. This location serves as both her creative and exhibition space, and she welcomes people to come enjoy a glass of wine, some music, or a friendly conversation while watching her work her magic. Shalimar generally holds seasonal exhibits where she features food and drinks from other local businesses and hopes you’ll join her at the next event. Please follow Art by Shalimar on Instagram or Facebook for daily inspiration and updates on her upcoming events!

properties.name: Art for Miles in the Blue Ridge Corridor
properties.description: The art in this area isn't limited to your typical portraits and pictures, although you can find that here, too! Visit artwork sites in the Blue Ridge Corridor, and you'll find everything from sprawling gardens and iconic statues to intricate displays of team pride.

properties.name: Artists Alliance of the Triangle
properties.description: Fuquay-Varina Arts Council's mission is to inspire and enhance the lives of citizens in the community and beyond by developing appreciation of the arts, presenting arts programming, supporting local artists and fostering creativity in the community.

properties.name: Arts Access Gallery
properties.description:
The new Arts Access Gallery in downtown Raleigh is dedicated to showcasing and selling the work of artists with disabilities — the only one in the region. The small, intimate space is the perfect venue to immerse yourself in a rotating slate of different artists throughout the year. Visitors will also get a chance to participate in free artist talks and related events.

The Arts Access gallery also has a permanent collection with pieces from artists such as acrylic painters Angela Dawson, Rachard McIntyre and Wiley Johnson.

properties.name: Arts N.C. State
properties.description: N.C. State University’s cultural offerings include music, dance and theatre performances, crafts classes and art exhibitions. All events and exhibitions are open to the public. Performance tickets are available through Ticket Central. Admission varies; call or visit website.

properties.name: Artspace
properties.description: Artspace is the only visual arts center in North Carolina with 30+ studio artists, three rotating exhibition spaces, education and community engagement programming. Drop by to meet inspiring local artists, purchase original artwork or take a class. There's a new exhibit and hands-on art activity every month! Free admission; donations appreciated. Hours: Wed-Sat., 11am-7pm; Sunday, 11am-4pm; First Friday of each month, 11am-10pm; studio hours vary.

properties.name: Block Gallery at Raleigh Municipal Building
properties.description: Connecting local artists to community through ongoing exhibitions and public outreach, the Office of Raleigh Arts’ Block Gallery is a gateway for artists to exhibit their work in a professional setting for a diverse audience. Free admission. Hours: Mon.-Fri., 8:30am-5:15pm.

properties.name: Cary Art Loop
properties.description:
Final Fridays, 6-9 p.m. 
Cary Art Loop highlights Triangle arts & culture in the Cary Area offering extended hours for participating art galleries, restaurants, coffee houses, and other businesses that showcase visual arts, music and more! 
For maps, details and more visit: www.caryartloop.org 
“The mission of the Cary Art Loop is to unite Cary’s diverse and growing community through the arts. The Cary Art Loop coordinates with Cary businesses to showcase the talents of local artists culminating in a public celebration on the final Fridays of each month. By fostering local art in all its forms, we enrich Cary.”

properties.name: Cary Arts Center
properties.description:
Cary Arts Center provides a vibrant and robust center for arts activity for the residents of Cary and continues the legacy of education begun on this site when Town of Cary founder Allison Frances Page opened Cary Academy in the 1870's. The approx. 48,000 square foot facility includes classrooms, studios, rehearsal, performance and office space for a wide range of visual, artisan and performing arts.


The center is home to the Town's Marvelous Music Series and Applause! Cary Youth Theatre and provides performance and programming space for the town's cultural organizations. The center provides a public rental program that includes the theatre and select rooms and spaces in the facility and an Open Studio Program that allows access to well-equipped artist studios.

properties.name: Cary Community Choir
properties.description: Cary Community Choir is a non-profit organization comprised of more than 100 singers and musicians from the community who come together annually for a performance of Handel's Messiah in Cary, N.C.

properties.name: Cary Gallery of Artists
properties.description: The Cary Gallery of Artists is a cooperative operated by local artists featuring contemporary and traditional fine art and craft, with more than 300 artworks exhibited by 20 plus artists from around the Raleigh area. Each day an artist is on duty. Displays change monthly, so there is always new work to enjoy when you visit. Since our founding in 2005, the Cary Gallery has offered affordable, high-quality original artwork with a wide array of pieces including jewelry, ceramics, paintings, fiber art and much more. Many of the artists who call the gallery "home" are well known—teaching, exhibiting, winning awards and appearing frequently in the press.

properties.name: Cary Town Band
properties.description: The Cary Town Band (Cary, NC) is reminiscent of the turn of the 20th century bands led by Sousa, Goldman, and others who popularized band concerts all over America. Presenting concerts recreating that bygone era, the band plays marches from many nations, circus music, waltzes, rags, polkas, famous overtures, and other “pops” classical music of the 1860’s to 1920’s with an occasional nod to more modern fare.

properties.name: Cary Visual Art, Inc.
properties.description: Over the years Cary Visual Art has placed more than 50 works of art, valued at more than $1 million at parks, businesses and public property across the Town of Cary. Sculpture and two-dimensional works by artists from all over the country are prominently placed in Cary's public buildings and open spaces. Cary Visual Art commissions the placement of public art, supports exhibitions and engages the community through sculpture tours, artist residencies, lectures and workshops. They view partnerships as an essential component of public art – by involving individuals, community groups and local businesses with the commissioning process, public art has greater impact, levels of appreciation and longevity. This comprehensive approach has provided a vast array of sites, types of artwork and community involvement.

properties.name: City Market Artist Collective
properties.description: City Market Artist Collective (CMAC) was created and founded by sculptor Paris Alexander in 2020. Paris invited a select group of resident artist to fill this large open gallery space with a variety of works, including paintings, sculpture and mixed media works. There are eight distinct galley spaces including a dedicated sculpture gallery. There is also a monthly invited guest artist exhibition.

properties.name: Code f.a.d Company
properties.description: Code f.a.d. Company (where f.a.d. in an acronym for film—art—dance) is a group of artists committed to combining film, visual art, and dance into precisely designed performance experiences. Code f.a.d. Company's mission is to create multimedia, movement-based artwork for performance and exhibition, enriching the community and the lives of artists and audiences; to educate youth and the greater community in the art of dance through performances and workshops in schools, community centers, and festivals; and to provide professional-level dance instruction to its members and qualified community participants.

properties.name: Crafts Center at North Carolina State University
properties.description: For over 40 years The Crafts Center has functioned as an art school specializing in crafts classes and workshops in art, pottery, sculpture, weaving, fiber arts, photography, woodworking, glass, jewelry, lapidary, and more.  NC State’s Crafts Center provides a friendly and informal learning environment for students and craftspeople of all levels in its state-of-the-art studio spaces.  It is considered to be one of the finest university crafts programs in the country.  Classes and studio use are available to NC State students, alumni, employees, and the general public.  The Crafts Center is located in the Frank Thompson Building on the NC State campus, at the corner of Dunn Avenue and Jensen Drive (directly across from the Coliseum Parking Deck).

properties.name: Expressions in Rhythm Studio
properties.description: Expressions in Rhythm Studio is a progressive technique performing arts studio in the heart of Raleigh, NC. Our mission is to enrich the lives of our students and community through the performing arts. Acro, African, Ballet, Djembe, Hip Hop, Jazz, Liturgical, Lyrical and Tap are some of the dance and music classes we offer in our positive learning environment.  We provide students of all skill levels a fun and positive atmosphere to learn and express the art of standing out through dance and music. Our training is worth the travel!

properties.name: Firebox Theatre Company
properties.description:
Firebox Theatre Company shares meaningful stories for the community while developing a culture of professional artists in Wake Forest, N.C. 

Located in a historic cotton warehouse in Downtown Wake Forest, The Graham Johnson Cultural Arts Center, aka "The Graham" now sits. It is a charming 65 seat black box theatre open to performing artists of all kinds and residency to Firebox Theatre Company. Audiences love sitting around the action as the performers play on an intimate 3/4 thrust stage. Firebox is dedicated to creating quality theatre experiences and this extends to community enriching programs, such as educational offerings for children. As a theatre company, our energy is generated by the art we make and the stories we share. Stories and experiences fuel us all. Come into the Firebox with us and be energized!

properties.name: Frameworks
properties.description: Frameworks Gallery and Frame Design is a locally owned and family-operated frame shop in Raleigh, North Carolina that specializes in museum-quality framing for art, photographs, portraits, memorabilia and much more. Frameworks strives to provide the best in picture framing and total customer service experience. Simply put, Frameworks stands behind their craftsmanship, products, and people 100%. Their philosophy is straightforward: “Frame it once, frame it right, and frame it forever. Things of quality have no fear of time!”

properties.name: Frankie G. Weems Gallery
properties.description: Meredith College's Frank G. Weems art gallery presents exhibitions with a rich diversity of visual, cultural, aesthetic and topical focuses to the college community, as well as the broader Triangle area. Visually inspiring and intellectually engaging shows in the gallery explore concepts such as language as art, women in prison, artists' inspirations, use of sustainable resources, the creative process and Afro-Atlantic costumes and masking. Photography, clay, textiles, painting, video, painting, drawing, mixed media, printmaking and installations are some of the expressive media and conceptual approaches that can be seen. Class, campus and public programs are offered to enrich exhibitions' visual content.

properties.name: Fuquay-Varina Arts Center
properties.description: The Fuquay-Varina Arts Center hosts a 294-seat theatre, complete with technical booth and performance support spaces, an art gallery, administrative offices, dance, painting and digital studios and four classrooms for a variety of visual and performing arts classes.

properties.name: Holly Springs Community Band
properties.description: The Holly Springs Community Band performs throughout the entire southwestern Wake County area. These musicians comprise an all-volunteer group of various backgrounds. HSCB members perform in order to foster an appreciation for every kind of band music. Past works include rock music renditions, marches, movie theme songs, semi-classical, and classical. Each concert boasts selections which appeal to every generation.

properties.name: Kennedy Theatre at Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts
properties.description: This 40' x 60' black-box, 170-seat, experimental theater fuses intimacy with energy, the deeply personal with the universal theater experience. The K.D. & Sara Lynn Kennedy Theatre provides performance space for innovative groups including Hot Summer Nights.

properties.name: LaMantia Gallery
properties.description: LaMantia Gallery is a fine art gallery specializing in internationally known artists with a focus on traditional and pop art. All work featured is for sale.

properties.name: Liz Kelly Pottery
properties.description: Liz Kelly Pottery produces small batch ceramics, handmade in Raleigh, N.C. Studio visits are welcome. The studio has a nice selection of pottery on-hand to shop or browse. Email to schedule a visit.

properties.name: Lump
properties.description: Lump is located in downtown Raleigh, N.C. Combining the rigor and professionalism of a commercial gallery with the experimental attitude of alternative spaces, they present exhibitions and projects with emerging, mid-career and under-recognized artists. With a fifteen year history, they remain committed to the exhibition of challenging and thought-provoking contemporary art that falls outside the confines of a commodity-driven art market.

properties.name: Meredith College Cultural Events
properties.description: Meredith College offers a number of public lectures by nationally known speakers, art exhibitions, music, dance and theatre performances that are open to the public. Call or visit website for specific information concerning dates, hours and admission.

properties.name: North Carolina Symphony
properties.description:
Founded in 1932, the North Carolina Symphony (NCS) is a vital and honored component of North Carolina’s cultural life. Each year, more than 300 concerts, education programs and community engagement offerings reach adults and schoolchildren in all 100 N.C. counties—in communities large and small, and in concert halls, auditoriums, gymnasiums, restaurants, clubs and outdoor settings. The NCS is proud to expand access to audiences around the globe through concerts and educational offerings available through the digital space.

NCS’s state headquarters venue is the spectacular Meymandi Concert Hall at the Martin Marietta Center for the Performing Arts in downtown Raleigh. The Symphony’s service across the state includes series in Chapel Hill, Wilmington, New Bern, Southern Pines and Fayetteville, as well as the Summerfest series at its summer home, the outdoor Koka Booth Amphitheatre in Cary. NCS brings some of the world’s greatest talents to N.C. and embraces home-state artists from classical musicians to bluegrass bands, creating live music experiences distinctive to N.C. NCS is dedicated to giving voice to new art and has presented more than 50 U.S. or world premieres in its history.

Committed to engaging students of all ages across N.C., NCS leads one of the most extensive education programs of any symphony orchestra in the country—serving over 100,000 students each year. In alignment with the curriculum set by the N.C. Department of Public Instruction, the Symphony provides training and resources for teachers, sends small ensembles into classrooms and presents full-orchestra in-person and online Education Concerts that bring the fundamentals of music to life. Music Discovery for preschoolers combines music with storytelling, and at the middle and high school levels, students have opportunities to work directly with NCS artists and perform for NCS audiences.

The first state-supported symphony in the country, NCS performs under the auspices of the N.C. Department of Natural and Cultural Resources, D. Reid Wilson, Secretary.

properties.name: Oak City Sound
properties.description: Winner of the 2010 Carolinas District Award for Top Chorus, the General Assembly Chorus is a men's chorus performing various events throughout the year. See website for details on upcoming events and performances.

properties.name: Piedmont Pottery
properties.description: Piedmont Pottery is located in Fuquay-Varina, N.C. Potters Jeff and Lisa Ross’s works reflect both traditional North Carolina and classical styles that are influenced by nature, Celtic mythology and Asian minimalism. Most of our unique and affordable pottery for the home and garden is made using locally sourced stoneware clays and oxidation fired.  Our jewelry is crafted using hand-made ceramic beads and pendants in styles ranging from formal to whimsical to fit your unique personality.  We also feature a variety of photography, paintings, sculpture, accessories, and gifts.  In our studio we offer classes in pottery making, photography, and other arts and crafts.

properties.name: Pocket Gallery
properties.description: Pocket Gallery is small gallery and working studio in downtown Raleigh, N.C.

properties.name: Pullen Arts Center
properties.description: Pullen Arts Center offers classes and workshops in pottery, jewelry making, painting, printmaking, glass arts, bookmaking and more, along with an expanded gallery space and spaces for events.

properties.name: Pure Life Theatre Company
properties.description: Pure Life Theatre Company is a diverse group of artists who exist to serve the community through exceptional theatrical experiences and life-giving performances that explore and nourish truth, hope, redemption and love.

properties.name: Raleigh ACT
properties.description: Raleigh ACT is the areas only exclusive children’s theatre offering a variety of artistic opportunities for children to discover and develop their talents. Students gain an appreciation for the arts and have a whole lot of fun being a star!

properties.name: Raleigh Area Flute Association
properties.description: The Raleigh Area Flute Association is a nonprofit corporation founded in 1985. It currently lists a membership roster of over 300 flutists. RAFA holds concerts and masterclasses with guest artists, workshops, recitals, scholarship competitions, flute choirs and an annual Flute Fair.

properties.name: Raleigh Drum Circle
properties.description: RDC is a community in rhythm. They are dedicated to using the universal language of percussive music and dance for creative self-expression. In doing so, they encourage cultural awareness, embrace diversity, and promote harmony through rhythm. Drumming for the Hoop Jam is Wednesday nights 6:30 - 8:30pm at Pullen Park (April thru October) and Winter Hoop Jam is Friday nights 6:30pm at Method Road Park (November thru March).

properties.name: Raleigh Flute Choir
properties.description: The Raleigh Flute Choir, a chamber ensemble of professional flutists from central North Carolina, was founded in 1986 and has distinguished itself as one of the nation's leading flute choirs. Utilizing all members of the flute family, they perform an exciting repertoire spanning the centuries from the Renaissance to the present, including transcriptions and original compositions. In addition to formal concerts, they fulfill their mission to both entertain and educate by performing for numerous community and private functions, often via a trio or quartet. As a major sponsor of the Raleigh Area Flute Association, the choir also supports masterclasses, recitals, amateur choirs, seminars, and scholarships for area flutists.

properties.name: Raleigh Jazz Orchestra
properties.description: The Raleigh Jazz Orchestra (RJO) was organized as a not for profit arts institution in January, 2003 in collaboration with the Raleigh Symphony to create professional performance opportunities for jazz musicians.
